docs.title: Device Lock/Unlock
docs.text: The UiAutomator2 driver allows interactions with the Android lock screen using various APIs.

docs.title: Available APIs
docs.text:
The driver provides several capabilities for unlocking the device screen on session startup:

  • appium:skipUnlock
  • appium:unlockType
  • appium:unlockKey
  • appium:unlockStrategy
  • appium:unlockSuccessTimeout

Additionally, the driver includes execute methods for locking or unlocking the device during the session:

  • mobile: lock
  • mobile: unlock
  • mobile: isLocked

docs.title: Unlock Types
docs.text: The above capabilities and execute methods support multiple unlock types, which change the expected format of the unlock key.

docs.title: pin
docs.text:
Can be used for PIN code-based lockscreens. The unlock key should match the PIN code and consist of its digits, for example 1111.

Under the hood, the driver simply searches for button elements matching each digit in the PIN code, and taps on them.

docs.title: pinWithKeyEvent
docs.text: Can be used for PIN code-based lockscreens. Equivalent to the pin type, but implemented by sending key events via adb instead.

docs.title: password
docs.text: Can be used for password-based lockscreens. The unlock key should match the password and consist of latin characters, for example abcd1234.

docs.title: pattern
docs.text:
Can be used for pattern-based lockscreens. The unlock key should be a sequence of digits, where each digit matches a pattern point, when ordered left-to-right, top-to-down.

For example, the unlock key in the following image is 729854163.

docs.title: fingerprint
docs.text: Can be used for fingerprint-based lockscreens. Only supported on emulators. The unlock key should be the identifier of the virtual fingerprint, similarly to the mobile: fingerprint execute method.

docs.title: BiDi Commands and Events
docs.text: The UiAutomator2 driver has partial support of the WebDriver BiDi Protocol. It inherits the BiDi commands and events supported by the Appium base driver, and additionally defines the events and commands listed below.

docs.title: log.entryAdded
docs.text:
WebDriver BiDi documentation: log.entryAdded

Indicates that a new log entry is available for consumption.

This event is emitted when the driver retrieves a new entry for any of the log types listed below.

Available since driver version 3.7.10.

docs.title: Event Type (CDDL)
docs.text:
log.entryAded = (
  context: text,
  method: "log.entryAdded",
  params: {
    type: text,
    level: "debug" / "info" / "warn" / "error",
    source: {
      realm: '',
      context: text,
    },
    text: text,
    timestamp: js-uint,
  },
)
Parameter Description context The context in which the log was created, usually either native or webview type One of the supported log types listed below text Contents of the log entry timestamp Timestamp of the log entry

docs.title: Supported Types
docs.text:
Event emission of all of these log types is supported for both real devices and emulators.

  • syslog
    • Each event contains a single device adb logcat line
    • context is always set to NATIVE_APP
    • Event emission can be disabled by setting the appium:skipLogcatCapture capability
  • server
    • Each event contains a single Appium server log line
    • context is always set to NATIVE_APP
    • Events are only emitted if the get_server_logs insecure feature is enabled

docs.title: appium:uiautomator2.contextUpdated
docs.text:
Indicates a change in the current Appium context.

This event is emitted upon context change, either explicit or implicit. It is also emitted at the start of a new session.

See the GitHub feature ticket for more details.

Available since driver version 3.9.5.

docs.title: Event Type (CDDL)
docs.text:
appium:uiautomator2.contextUpdated = (
  method: "appium:uiautomator2.contextUpdated",
  params: {
    name: text,
    type: "NATIVE" / "WEB",
  },
)
Parameter Description name The name of the new context type The type of the currently active context. Supported values are NATIVE or WEB.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
This page lists various capabilities used and implemented by the UiAutomator2 driver. To learn more about capabilities, refer to the Appium documentation.

For other capabilities recognized by the Appium server, see their Appium docs reference page.

docs.title: Standard
docs.text: Refer to the W3C WebDriver documentation for more information about these capabilities.

docs.title: platformName
docs.text:
Name Type Default platformName string Not specified

May be set to android. Appium is not strict about this value if the appium:automationName capability is provided, so feel free to assign it to any platform name required, for example, for Selenium Grid compatibility.

docs.title: browserName
docs.text:
Name Type Default browserName string Not specified

If provided, the driver will try to start the test in web context mode, instead of the default native mode. Refer to the Hybrid Mode guide for more details. Can usually be set to chrome.

Do not set this capability in combination with either appium:app or appium:appPackage.

docs.title: pageLoadStrategy
docs.text: Name Type Default pageLoadStrategy string normal

docs.title: automationName
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:automationName string Not specified

Specifies the Appium driver to use. Must be set to UiAutomator2 (case-insensitive)

docs.title: deviceName
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:deviceName string Not specified

The name of the device under test. Not used to select a device under test - use appium:udid for real devices and appium:avd for emulators.

docs.title: platformVersion
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:platformVersion string Not specified

The platform version of the device under test. Used for device selection if appium:udid or appium:avd is not provided.

docs.title: udid
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:udid string Not specified

UDID of the device under test. Can be retrieved by running adb devices. If neither this capability nor appium:avd is set, the driver will automatically try to use the first connected device. Always set this capability when running parallel tests.

docs.title: skipDeviceInitialization
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:skipDeviceInitialization boolean false

Whether to skip the device initialization phase of session creation, such as checking if the device is available, installing the Appium Settings helper, adjusting permissions, etc... Can be useful if a session had already been previously started, and all the device setup steps were already completed.

docs.title: skipSettingsAppReinstall
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:skipSettingsAppReinstall boolean false

Whether to skip installation of the Appium Settings helper application (io.appium.settings) upon session start. Can be useful for environments where this application is provisioned separately.

Available since driver version 8.1.1.

docs.title: skipLogcatCapture
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:skipLogcatCapture boolean false

Whether to skip collecting device logcat logs.

docs.title: clearDeviceLogsOnStart
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:clearDeviceLogsOnStart boolean false

Whether device logs should be cleared upon session start. Maps to the -c flag of adb logcat.

docs.title: logcatFormat
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:logcatFormat string threadtime

The output format of device logcat logs. Maps to the -v flag of adb logcat. Refer to the logcat documentation for supported values.

docs.title: logcatFilterSpecs
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:logcatFilterSpecs string or Array<string> Not specified

One or more filter expressions to use for filtering device logcat output. Refer to the logcat documentation for the format of a filter expression.

docs.title: ignoreHiddenApiPolicyError
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:ignoreHiddenApiPolicyError boolean false

Whether to ignore failures caused by the driver automatically relaxing Android's hidden API access policies, in order to enable access to non-SDK interfaces (such as logging). May be useful on devices where access to these policies has been locked by its vendor.

docs.title: disableSuppressAccessibilityService
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:disableSuppressAccessibilityService boolean false

Whether the instrumentation process should avoid suppressing accessibility services during the session. Useful if your automated test needs these services.

docs.title: disableWindowAnimation
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:disableWindowAnimation boolean true

Whether to disable window animations. Google recommends disabling animations when running automated tests, in order to avoid flakiness. The animation state is automatically restored after the session is stopped, unless the session is ended unexpectedly, for Android 7 (Nougat / API level 25) or older.

docs.title: language
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:language string Not specified

Language code to use for setting the locale of the device under test. The code should match the language field for Android's Locale class. Must be provided together with appium:locale.

The language set by this capability is also used by the mobile: getAppStrings execute method, unless explicitly overridden.

docs.title: locale
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:locale string Not specified

Country code to use for setting the locale of the device under test. The code should match the country field for Android's Locale class. Must be provided together with appium:language.

docs.title: localeScript
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:localeScript string Not specified

Script code to use for setting the locale of the device under test. The code should match the script field for Android's Locale class. If specified, appium:language and appium:locale must also be provided.

docs.title: timeZone
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:timeZone string Not specified

Value used to override the current timezone of the device. Persists until the next override. Must be a valid TZ identifier.

Available since driver version 3.1.0.

docs.title: hideKeyboard
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:hideKeyboard boolean Not specified

Whether to hide the on-screen keyboard during the session. This is achieved by creating a custom "artificial" input method. It is recommended to use this feature only for special/exploratory cases, as it violates the way a user normally interacts with the application under test.

If explicitly set to false, adb shell ime reset is run on session startup, which resets the currently selected/enabled IMEs to the default ones, as if the device was initially booted with the current locale.

Available since driver version 2.33.0.

docs.title: orientation
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:orientation string Not specified

Orientation to set for the device under test upon session start. Supported values are PORTRAIT and LANDSCAPE. Using this capability is equivalent to calling the setAppiumOrientation endpoint.

docs.title: gpsEnabled
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:gpsEnabled boolean Not specified

Whether to enable or disable location services (GPS) upon session start. This functionality only works reliably starting from Android 12 (S / API level 31).

docs.title: mockLocationApp
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:mockLocationApp string io.appium.settings

Package identifier of the app to use for mocking device location. Has no effect on emulators. If set to null or an empty string, Appium will skip the setup of the location mocking feature.

docs.title: skipUnlock
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:skipUnlock boolean Not specified

Whether to skip automatically unlocking the device lockscreen on session startup, if one is present. Since the unlocking process takes time, it is recommended to set this capability to true and disable screen locking on the device(s) under test.

docs.title: unlockType
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:unlockType string Not specified

The type of lockscreen security on the device, which can be used to unlock it. If omitted, the driver assumes no security is used, and the screen can be unlocked without additional details.

Supported values are pin, password, and pattern. Must be provided together with appium:unlockKey, whose value depends on the lockscreen type.

Refer to the Device Lock/Unlock guide for more details.

docs.title: unlockKey
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:unlockKey string Not specified

The key used to unlock the lockscreen. The expected format depends on the value of appium:unlockType, which must be provided together with this capability. If omitted, the driver assumes no security is used, and the screen can be unlocked without additional details.

Refer to the Device Lock/Unlock guide for more details.

docs.title: unlockStrategy
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:unlockStrategy string Not specified

The approach to use for unlocking the screen. Supported values are locksettings and uiautomator. The appium:unlockKey and appium:unlockType must be provided in order for this capability to take effect.

By default, or if set to locksettings, unlocking is done using adb-based fast unlock. If set to uiautomator, the unlock approach depends on the appium:unlockType capability.

docs.title: unlockSuccessTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:unlockSuccessTimeout integer 2000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait until the device is unlocked.

docs.title: avd
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:avd string Not specified

The name of Android emulator to run the test on. The names of currently installed emulators can be listed by running avdmanager list avd. If the specified emulator is not running upon starting a session, the driver will automatically launch it.

docs.title: avdLaunchTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:avdLaunchTimeout integer 60000

Maximum number in milliseconds to wait until the Android emulator has started.

docs.title: avdReadyTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:avdReadyTimeout integer 60000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait until the Android emulator has fully booted and is ready for usage.

docs.title: avdArgs
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:avdArgs string or Array<string> Not specified

One or more supported command-line arguments to apply when starting the emulator. Only applied if the emulator is not already running.

docs.title: avdEnv
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:avdEnv Record<string, any> Not specified

One or more environment variables to set when starting the emulator. Only applied if the emulator is not already running.

docs.title: isHeadless
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:isHeadless boolean false

Whether to start the emulator in headless mode. Maps to the -no-window emulator command-line argument. Only applied if the emulator is not already running.

docs.title: allowDelayAdb
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:allowDelayAdb boolean true

Whether to wait until the emulator has finished booting before processing ADB packets. Maps to the -delay-adb flag of adb. Requires emulator version 29.0.7 or later, running Android 9 (Pie / API level 28) or later.

Refer to this issue for more details.

docs.title: networkSpeed
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:networkSpeed string Not specified

The network speed to apply to the emulator. Maps to the -netspeed emulator command-line argument. Only applied if the emulator is not already running.

docs.title: injectedImageProperties
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:injectedImageProperties Record<string, Record<string, number>> Not specified

Adjusts properties of the image injected using the mobile: injectEmulatorCameraImage execute method. If the emulator is already running, it will be restarted in order to apply the properties.

The value of this capability is an object with the following keys. All keys and sub-keys are optional, with the given defaults used for absent keys.

Key Description Default size Scale multipliers for X and Y axes {scaleX: 1, scaleY: 1} position Offset coefficients for X/Y/Z axes, where 0 means centered {x: 0, y: 0, z: -1.5} rotation Degrees of rotation for X/Y/Z axes {x: 0, y: 0, z: 0}

Available since driver version 3.6.0.

docs.title: adbPort
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:adbPort integer 5037

Number of the port to use for starting ADB. Maps to the -P flag of adb.

docs.title: remoteAdbHost
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:remoteAdbHost string localhost

Name of the ADB server host. Maps to the -H flag of adb.

docs.title: adbExecTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:adbExecTimeout integer 20000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait for the execution of any single ADB command.

docs.title: buildToolsVersion
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:buildToolsVersion string Not specified

The version of Android build tools to use (name of a directory located at $ANDROID_HOME/build-tools). By default, the driver uses the most recent available version, but it may be useful to explicitly change this in case of any known bugs.

docs.title: allowOfflineDevices
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:allowOfflineDevices boolean false

Whether to include offline devices in the list of devices returned by ADB.

docs.title: suppressKillServer
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:suppressKillServer boolean false

Whether to prevent the driver from ever killing the ADB server. Can be useful if ADB is connected wirelessly.

docs.title: adbListenAllNetwork
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:adbListenAllNetwork boolean false

Whether to listen on all network interfaces, not only localhost. Maps to the -a flag of adb. The adb_listen_all_network insecure feature must be enabled.

Available since driver version 6.7.0.

docs.title: systemPort
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:systemPort integer 8200

The port on the host machine where the UiAutomator2 server should be listening. Must be unique for each session - see the Testing in Parallel guide for details. If not provided, Appium will try the first available port in the range [8200, 8299].

On the device under test, the UiAutomator2 server port can be configured using the serverPort setting.

docs.title: uiautomator2ServerInstallTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:uiautomator2ServerInstallTimeout integer 20000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait until the UiAutomator2 server application is installed on the device under test.

docs.title: uiautomator2ServerLaunchTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:uiautomator2ServerLaunchTimeout integer 30000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait until the UiAutomator2 server application on the device under test has started.

docs.title: uiautomator2ServerReadTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:uiautomator2ServerReadTimeout integer 240000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait for a response for a request to the UiAutomator2 server. Must be greater than 0.

docs.title: skipServerInstallation
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:skipServerInstallation boolean false

Whether to skip installation of the UiAutomator2 server on the device under test, along with all other related checks. Useful for speeding up session startup if the device already has a compatible UiAutomator2 server app installed. Note that unexpected errors may occur if the UiAutomator2 server app is not compatible with the driver or the app under test.

docs.title: mjpegServerPort
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:mjpegServerPort integer Not specified

The port on the host machine where the MJPEG screenshot streaming server should be listening. If not specified, the MJPEG stream from the device under test is not forwarded. Can be used to connect to the device MJPEG stream outside of the session.

On the device under test, the MJPEG server port can be configured using the mjpegServerPort setting.

Refer to the MJPEG guide for more details.

docs.title: mjpegScreenshotUrl
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:mjpegScreenshotUrl string Not specified

URL of a service that provides realtime device screenshots in MJPEG format. If provided, screenshot retrieval will request images from this service rather than using the default screenshot mechanism.

Refer to the MJPEG guide for more details.

docs.title: app
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:app string Not specified

Full path to a file on the host machine, or URL to a remote location, that contains the application under test. The app file must have either the .apk or .apks extension.

Do not set this capability in combination with browserName.

This capability is always required for driver versions 2.31.2 or earlier.

docs.title: appPackage
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appPackage string Not specified

Package identifier of the application under test. Can be provided in combination with appium:app, but if only appium:app is provided, the package identifier is automatically detected from the app manifest.

Do not set this capability in combination with browserName.

Refer to the Activity Startup guide for more details.

docs.title: appActivity
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appActivity string Not specified

Launchable activity identifier of the application under test. If not provided, the activity is automatically detected from either appium:app or appium:appPackage, in that order.

Refer to the Activity Startup guide for more details.

docs.title: appWaitPackage
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appWaitPackage string Matches the package identifier (see appium:appPackage)

Identifier of the first app package to be launched.

Refer to the Activity Startup guide for more details.

docs.title: appWaitActivity
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appWaitActivity string Matches the app main activity (see appium:appActivity)

Identifier of the first app activity to be launched.

Refer to the Activity Startup guide for more details.

docs.title: appWaitForLaunch
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appWaitForLaunch boolean true

When launching the app under test, whether to wait until the app has started (specifically, once Android's Activity Manager returns control to the driver). By default, the driver always waits up to the amount of time specified by appium:appWaitDuration. Setting this capability to false returns control as soon as Activity Manager successfully triggers the activity start command.

Refer to the Activity Startup guide for more details.

docs.title: appWaitDuration
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:appWaitDuration integer 20000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait until the activity specified by appium:appWaitPackage and appium:appWaitActivity has started.

Refer to the Activity Startup guide for more details.

docs.title: intentCategory
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:intentCategory string android.intent.category.LAUNCHER (CATEGORY_LAUNCHER)

Intent category to apply when launching the app. Refer to the Android Intent documentation for a list of possible values (prefixed with CATEGORY_).

Can also be specified using the mobile: startActivity execute method.

docs.title: intentAction
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:intentAction string android.intent.action.MAIN (ACTION_MAIN)

Intent action to apply when launching the app. Refer to the Android Intent documentation for a list of possible values (prefixed with ACTION_).

Can also be specified using the mobile: startActivity execute method.

docs.title: intentFlags
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:intentFlags string 0x10200000 (FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK and FLAG_ACTIVITY_RESET_TASK_IF_NEEDED)

Intent flags to apply when launching the app. Refer to the Android Intent documentation for a list of possible values (prefixed with FLAG_).

Can also be specified using the mobile: startActivity execute method.

docs.title: optionalIntentArguments
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:optionalIntentArguments string Not specified

Space-separated string of one or more intent arguments to apply to the launchable activity. The format should be -flag1 key1, -flag2 key2 value2, or a combination like -flag1 key1 -flag2 key2 value2.

docs.title: androidInstallTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:androidInstallTimeout integer 90000

Maximum amount of milliseconds to wait until the application under test is installed.

docs.title: enforceAppInstall
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:enforceAppInstall boolean Not specified

Whether to always reinstall the application under test, even if a newer version already exists on the device under test.

Has no effect if either appium:noReset or appium:fullReset is set.

docs.title: noReset
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:noReset boolean Not specified

Whether to prevent the app from being automatically relaunched and its data cleaned before session startup.

Mutually exclusive with appium:fullReset.

docs.title: fullReset
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:fullReset boolean false

Whether to always reinstall the app before session startup, and uninstall it after deleting the session.

Mutually exclusive with appium:noReset.

docs.title: dontStopAppOnReset
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:dontStopAppOnReset boolean Not specified

Whether to skip termination of the app under test upon session deletion, as well as upon session start, in case the app is already running.

docs.title: autoLaunch
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:autoLaunch boolean true

Whether to launch the application under test on session start, and wait until it is ready.

docs.title: forceAppLaunch
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:forceAppLaunch boolean Not specified

Whether to relaunch the app upon session startup even if appium:noReset is set.

Available since driver version 2.12.0.

docs.title: shouldTerminateApp
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:shouldTerminateApp boolean Not specified

Whether to stop the app upon session deletion even if appium:noReset is set.

Available since driver version 2.14.0.

docs.title: autoGrantPermissions
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:autoGrantPermissions boolean Not specified

Whether to automatically grant all requested application permissions upon session startup.

If the targetSdk of the application under test is below 23, or the device under test is running Android 5 (Lollipop / API level 22), granting permissions requires the application to be reinstalled, for example, using the appium:fullReset capability.

If the application requires some special security permissions (e.g. access to notifications or media recording), they can be changed using the mobile: changePermissions execute method with appops target.

docs.title: userProfile
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:userProfile integer Not specified

Identifier of a user profile used when launching the app under test. By default, the app is launched using the currently active user.

docs.title: otherApps
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:otherApps string or Array<string> Not specified

One or more application packages (either filepaths on the host machine, or URLs to remote locations) that should be installed on the device along with the application under test. The app files must have either the .apk or .apks extension.

docs.title: uninstallOtherPackages
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:uninstallOtherPackages string or Array<string> Not specified

One or more package identifiers to be uninstalled from the device upon session startup. Always excludes packages required by the driver (io.appium.settings, io.appium.uiautomator2.server, and io.appium.uiautomator2.server.test).

docs.title: allowTestPackages
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:allowTestPackages boolean Not specified

Whether to allow installation of test-only versions of the application under test. Maps to the -t flag of adb install. Only applied if the application is to be installed or reinstalled.

docs.title: remoteAppsCacheLimit
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:remoteAppsCacheLimit integer 10

Maximum number of application packages to be cached on the device under test. Primarily needed for devices that don't support streamed installs (Android 7 and below), which require adb to push each installable package to the device first, requiring additional time.

If set to 0, the cache is disabled.

docs.title: useKeystore
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:useKeystore boolean Not specified

Whether to use a custom keystore to sign the app under test. By default, apps are signed with the default Appium debug certificate, unless appium:noSign is used.

Used in combination with appium:keystorePath, appium:keystorePassword, appium:keyAlias and appium:keyPassword.

docs.title: keystorePath
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:keystorePath string Not specified

Full path to the keystore file on the server filesystem.

Used in combination with appium:useKeystore, appium:keystorePassword, appium:keyAlias and appium:keyPassword.

docs.title: keystorePassword
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:keystorePassword string Not specified

Password of the keystore file specified by appium:keystorePath.

Used in combination with appium:useKeystore, appium:keystorePath, appium:keyAlias and appium:keyPassword.

docs.title: keyAlias
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:keyAlias string Not specified

Alias of the key in the keystore file specified by appium:keystorePath.

Used in combination with appium:useKeystore, appium:keystorePath, appium:keystorePassword and appium:keyPassword.

docs.title: keyPassword
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:keyAlias string Not specified

Password of the key in the keystore file specified by appium:keystorePath.

Used in combination with appium:useKeystore, appium:keystorePath, appium:keystorePassword and appium:keyAlias.

docs.title: noSign
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:noSign boolean false

Whether to skip signing of the application under test, and use it as-is. By default, all apps are signed with the default Appium debug signature.

This capability does not affect .apks packages, as they are expected to be already signed.

docs.title: autoWebview
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:autoWebview boolean Not specified

Whether to automatically switch to a webview context upon session start. The name of the selected context is derived from the application package, prefixed by WEBVIEW_, but can be changed using the appium:autoWebviewName capability.

docs.title: autoWebviewName
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:autoWebviewName string Not specified

Custom name of a webview context, used to replace the application package part of the initial webview name used by appium:autoWebview.

Available since driver version 2.10.0.

docs.title: autoWebviewTimeout
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:autoWebviewTimeout integer 2000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait until a webview is available before switching to it. Has no effect unless appium:autoWebview is set.

docs.title: androidDeviceSocket
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:androidDeviceSocket string Not specified

Name of a Chromium DevTools socket on the device under test. If set, webview discovery will only return webviews running on this socket.

docs.title: webviewDevtoolsPort
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:webviewDevtoolsPort integer 10900

The port to use for communicating with webviews over the DevTools protocol. Must be unique for each session - see the Testing in Parallel guide for details. If not provided, Appium will try the first available port in the range [10900, 11000].

docs.title: ensureWebviewsHavePages
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:ensureWebviewsHavePages boolean true

Whether to skip web views that have no pages from being included in the list of available contexts. The driver uses the DevTools connection to retrieve information about existing pages.

docs.title: enableWebviewDetailsCollection
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:enableWebviewDetailsCollection boolean true

Whether to retrieve extended webview information via DevTools. Enabling this capability improves detection of the required ChromeDriver version.

docs.title: chromeOptions
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromeOptions Record<string, any> Not specified

Map of ChromeDriver options to apply. Refer to Google's ChromeOptions documentation for supported values.

docs.title: chromeLoggingPrefs
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromeLoggingPrefs Record<string, string> {"browser": "ALL"}

Map of logging types to their levels that should be applied. Refer to Selenium's Logging documentation for supported type and level values.

docs.title: chromedriverPort
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverPort integer Random

The port to use for ChromeDriver communication. Must be unique for each session - see the Testing in Parallel guide for details. By default, a random free port is used.

docs.title: chromedriverPorts
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverPort Array<number | Array<number>> Not specified

List of possible ports and/or port ranges to use for ChromeDriver communication, for example, [5600, 5610, [5650, 5660]]. An error is thrown if all specified ports are busy.

docs.title: chromedriverArgs
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverArgs Array<string> Not specified

List of command line switches to apply to ChromeDriver. Refer to the links in Selenium's Chrome documentation for more details on supported switches. Note that not all desktop Chrome switches are available on mobile.

docs.title: chromedriverExecutable
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverExecutable string Not specified

Custom path to a ChromeDriver executable on the host file system. Takes priority over appium:chromedriverExecutableDir.

Refer to the Managing ChromeDriver guide for more details.

docs.title: chromedriverExecutableDir
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverExecutableDir string See below

Custom path to a directory on the host file system, containing ChromeDriver executables. If automatic ChromeDriver download is enabled, this folder is also used to store the downloaded executables.

The default value is node_modules/appium-chromedriver/chromedriver/<host os> in the driver's installation directory.

Refer to the Managing ChromeDriver guide for more details.

docs.title: chromedriverChromeMappingFile
chromedriverUseSystemExecutable
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverUseSystemExecutable boolean false

Whether to use the ChromeDriver binary bundled with the driver.

This capability is primarily relevant for driver versions 3.7.11 or earlier, which automatically downloaded ChromeDriver upon installation.

docs.title: chromedriverDisableBuildCheck
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverDisableBuildCheck boolean false

Whether to disable the check that requires ChromeDriver and the browser executable to have matching versions. Maps to the --disable-build-check flag of the ChromeDriver binary.

docs.title: chromedriverForwardBiDi
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverForwardBiDi boolean false

Whether to automatically forward the ChromeDriver BiDi web socket to the UiAutomator2 driver web socket. This allows sending browser-specific BiDi commands in a webview context. Switching the session context terminates this connection. Requires the BiDi protocol to be enabled (webSocketUrl capability must be true).

Note that older ChromeDriver versions may only have partial to no support for the BiDi protocol.

Available since driver version 6.1.0.

docs.title: chromedriverGrantPermissions
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:chromedriverGrantPermissions boolean false

Whether to automatically grant all requested runtime permissions for the Chrome/webview package, so that the session is not interrupted by any native runtime permission dialogs.

Available since driver version 8.1.0.

docs.title: recreateChromeDriverSessions
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:recreateChromeDriverSessions boolean false

Whether the driver should kill the ChromeDriver session upon switching to native context and recreate it upon switching back, instead of merely suspending it.

docs.title: nativeWebScreenshot
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:nativeWebScreenshot boolean false

Whether to use the screenshoting endpoint provided by the UI Automator framework instead of the one provided by ChromeDriver. Can be useful if experiencing issues with the latter.

docs.title: extractChromeAndroidPackageFromContextName
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:extractChromeAndroidPackageFromContextName boolean false

Whether to instruct ChromeDriver to attach to the Android package included in the context name, rather than the package of the application under test.

docs.title: showChromedriverLog
docs.text:
Name Type Default appium:showChromedriverLog boolean false

Whether to include ChromeDriver logs in Appium server logs.

docs.title: Element Attributes
docs.text:
The UiAutomator2 driver supports various native and custom element attributes.

As a general rule, attributes that have a null value, or are not applicable to a given element type or Android version, are omitted from the page source. One exception to this rule is text. Certain attributes also have further conditions for being omitted.

docs.title: a11y-focused
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is accessibility focused. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isAccessibilityFocused().

This attribute can also be retrieved using the accessibilityFocused alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: a11y-important
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is considered important for accessibility. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isImportantForAccessibility(). Supported since Android 7 (Nougat / API level 24).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the importantForAccessibility alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: actions
docs.text:
Example: ACTION_FOCUS,ACTION_SELECT,ACTION_CLEAR_SELECTION

Comma-separated list of constants identifying the element's available accessibility actions. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getActionList().

This attribute is not included in the default page source due to performance reasons, but it can be added by changing the includeA11yActionsInPageSource setting to true, or retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: bounds
docs.text:
Example: [0,0][100,100]

Bounds of the element's frame as a combination of its top-left and bottom-right corner points, formatted as [<top-left-X>,<top-left-Y>][<bottom-right-X>,<bottom-right-Y>]. Calculated by retrieving AccessibilityNodeInfo.getBoundsInScreen() and trimming the outer bounds.

docs.title: checkable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is checkable. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isCheckable().

docs.title: checked
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is checked. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isChecked(). Always set to false if checkable is false.

docs.title: class
docs.text:
Example: android.view.View

Full name of the element's class. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getClassName(). Could be null and therefore omitted.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the className alias.

docs.title: clickable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element responds to clicks. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isClickable().

docs.title: collection-info
docs.text:
Example: {"rowCount":5,"columnCount":1,"isHierarchical":false,"selectionMode":0}

JSON representation of the element's CollectionInfo, containing the rowCount, columnCount, isHierarchical, and selectionMode properties.

This attribute is not included in the default page source, but it can be retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint. Could be null if the element is not a collection.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the collectionInfo alias.

Available since driver version 8.3.0.

docs.title: collection-item-info
docs.text:
Example: {"rowIndex":2,"columnIndex":0,"rowSpan":1,"columnSpan":1,"isHeading":false,"isSelected":true,"rowTitle":null,"columnTitle":null}

JSON representation of the element's CollectionItemInfo, containing the rowIndex, columnIndex, rowSpan, columnSpan, isHeading, isSelected, rowTitle, and columnTitle properties. The isSelected property is supported since Android 11 (R / API level 30), while rowTitle and columnTitle are supported since Android 13 (Tiramisu / API level 33).

This attribute is not included in the default page source, but it can be retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint. Could be null if the element is not a collection item.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the collectionItemInfo alias.

Available since driver version 8.3.0.

docs.title: content-desc
docs.text:
Example: foo

Content description of the element. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getContentDescription(). Could be null and therefore omitted.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the contentDescription alias.

In applications written using React Native, this attribute reflects the value of the accessibilityLabel property.

docs.title: content-invalid
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the content of this element is invalid, e.g. a date that is not well-formed. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isContentInvalid().

This attribute can also be retrieved using the contentInvalid alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: contentSize
docs.text:
Example: {"left": 0, "top":0, "width": 100, "height": 100, "scrollableOffset": 10, "touchPadding": 0}

JSON representation of the dimensions and scroll-related properties of an element. Only applicable to scrollable views - use bounds to retrieve the element dimensions regardless of the element type.

This attribute is not included in the default page source due to performance reasons, but it can be retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint.

docs.title: context-clickable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is context clickable. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isContextClickable(). Supported since Android 6 (Marshmallow / API level 23).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the contextClickable alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: dismissable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element can be dismissed. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isDismissable().

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: displayed
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is visible to the user. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isVisibleToUser().

docs.title: drawing-order
docs.text:
Example: 3

Drawing order of the view corresponding to this element, relative to its siblings. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getDrawingOrder(). Supported since Android 7 (Nougat / API level 24).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the drawingOrder alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is enabled. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isEnabled().

docs.title: error
docs.text:
Example: there was an error!

Error text of the element. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getError().

This attribute can also be retrieved using the errorText alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: extras
docs.text:
Example: AccessibilityNodeInfo.roleDescription=;ACTION_ARGUMENT_HTML_ELEMENT_STRING_VALUES=ARTICLE,BLOCKQUOTE

Extra data of the element. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getExtras().

The value of this attribute is formatted as a semicolon-separated (;) string of key-value pairs, which in turn are separated using the equality sign (=). Keys with non-null but otherwise empty values are preserved.

This attribute is not included in the default page source due to performance reasons, but it can be added by changing the includeExtrasInPageSource setting to true, or retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint.

Available since driver version 2.1.0.

docs.title: focusable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is focusable. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isFocusable().

docs.title: focused
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is focused. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isFocused(). Always set to false if focusable is false.

docs.title: heading
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether element represents a heading. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isHeading(). Supported since Android 9 (Pie / API level 28).

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: hint
docs.text:
Example: enter text here

Hint text of the element. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getHintText(). Supported since Android 8 (Oreo / API level 26).

Available since driver version 2.0.4.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
Example: 1

Index of the element under its parent, relative to its siblings.

This attribute cannot be retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint.

docs.title: input-type
docs.text:
Example: 16

Integer bitmask of the element's input type. Only available for editable input text elements. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getInputType().

This attribute is omitted from the page source if its value is 0 (TYPE_NUMBER_VARIATION_NORMAL).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the inputType alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: is-collection
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element represents a collection container (e.g. a list or grid). Calculated by retrieving AccessibilityNodeInfo.getCollectionInfo() and checking whether it is not null.

This attribute is only included in the page source if its value is true.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the isCollection alias.

Available since driver version 8.3.0.

docs.title: is-collection-item
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element represents an item within a collection container (e.g. a list or grid). Calculated by retrieving AccessibilityNodeInfo.getCollectionItemInfo() and checking whether it is not null.

This attribute is only included in the page source if its value is true.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the isCollectionItem alias.

Available since driver version 8.3.0.

docs.title: live-region
docs.text:
Example: 1

Integer value of the element's live region mode. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getLiveRegion().

This attribute can also be retrieved using the liveRegion alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: long-clickable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element responds to long clicks. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isLongClickable().

This attribute can also be retrieved using the longClickable alias.

docs.title: max-text-length
docs.text:
Example: 30

Maximum text length for the element. Only available for input text elements. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getMaxTextLength().

This attribute is omitted from the page source if its value is -1 (maximum text length is not set).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the maxTextLength alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: multiline
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is a multi line editable text element. Only available for input text elements. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isMultiLine().

This attribute is omitted from the page source if the value of max-text-length is -1.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the multiLine alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: package
docs.text:
Example: com.mycompany

Identifier of the package the element belongs to. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getPackageName(). Could be null and therefore omitted.

docs.title: pane-title
docs.text:
Example: title

Title of the pane represented by this element. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getPaneTitle(). Supported since Android 9 (Pie / API level 28).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the paneTitle alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: password
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is a password input field. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isPassword().

docs.title: resource-id
docs.text:
Example: com.mycompany:id/resId

Fully qualified resource identifier of the element. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getViewIdResourceName(). Could be null and therefore omitted.

If the mapTestTagToResourceId setting is enabled, the value of this attribute is instead retrieved from the element's Jetpack Compose testTag property (androidx.compose.ui.semantics.testTag), if one is present.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the resourceId alias.

docs.title: screen-reader-focusable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is explicitly marked as a focusable unit by a screen reader. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isScreenReaderFocusable(). Supported since Android 9 (Pie / API level 28).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the screenReaderFocusable alias.

docs.title: scrollable
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is scrollable. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isScrollable().

docs.title: selected
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element is selected. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isSelected().

docs.title: selection-end
docs.text:
Example: 7

Index of the character where text selection ends. Only available for input text elements. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getTextSelectionEnd().

This attribute is omitted from the page source if no text is selected, or the element provides no range info.

docs.title: selection-start
docs.text:
Example: 3

Index of the character where text selection starts. Only available for input text elements. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getTextSelectionStart().

This attribute is omitted from the page source if no text is selected, or the element provides no range info.

docs.title: showing-hint
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element's text represents a hint for the user to enter text. Only available for editable input text elements. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isShowingHintText(). Supported since Android 8 (Oreo / API level 26).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the showingHintText alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: text
docs.text:
Example: some text

Text or value of the element, depending on the element type:

  • Range: retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.RangeInfo.getCurrent()
  • All other elements: retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getText()

The value of this attribute is never null - empty values are instead set to an empty string.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the name alias.

docs.title: text-entry-key
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element represents a text entry key that is part of a keyboard or keypad. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.isTextEntryKey(). Supported since Android 10 (Q / API level 29).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the textEntryKey alias.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: text-has-clickable-span
docs.text:
Example: true

Whether the element contains ClickableSpan or URLSpan markup elements. Retrieved from Spanned.getSpans(). Only available for text elements.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the textHasClickableSpan alias.

Available since driver version 4.2.7.

docs.title: text-size
docs.text:
Example: 12.6

Text size of the element, in units specified by text-unit. Only available for text elements. Calculated by retrieving AccessibilityNodeInfo.ExtraRenderingInfo.getTextSizeInPx() and scaling it according to text-unit. Supported since Android 11 (R / API level 30).

This attribute is not included in the default page source due to performance reasons, but it can be added by changing the includeExtraRenderingInfo setting to true, or retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the textSize alias.

Available since driver version 6.7.10.

docs.title: text-unit
docs.text:
Example: mm

Text size unit of the element. Only available for text elements. Calculated by retrieving AccessibilityNodeInfo.ExtraRenderingInfo.getTextSizeUnit() and converting it to a 2-character string. Supported since Android 11 (R / API level 30).

Supported values are:

  • dp - device independent pixels (COMPLEX_UNIT_DIP)
  • in - inches (COMPLEX_UNIT_IN)
  • mm - millimeters (COMPLEX_UNIT_MM)
  • pt - points (COMPLEX_UNIT_PT)
  • px - pixels (COMPLEX_UNIT_PX)
  • sp - scaled pixels (COMPLEX_UNIT_SP)

This attribute is not included in the default page source due to performance reasons, but it can be added by changing the includeExtraRenderingInfo setting to true, or retrieved using the standard Get Element Attribute endpoint.

This attribute can also be retrieved using the textUnit alias.

Available since driver version 6.7.10.

docs.title: tooltip-text
docs.text:
Example: Paste

Tooltip text of the element. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getTooltipText(). Supported since Android 9 (Pie / API level 28).

This attribute can also be retrieved using the tooltipText alias.

Available since driver version 4.2.7.

docs.title: window-id
docs.text:
Example: 123

Identifier of the window this element belongs to. Retrieved from AccessibilityNodeInfo.getWindowId().

This attribute can also be retrieved using the windowId alias.

Available since driver version 6.4.1.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
The UiAutomator2 driver comes with a set of many available endpoints, which are primarily inherited from the Appium base driver, and can be found in their Appium docs reference pages. Refer to the documentation of your Appium client for how to call specific endpoints.

The driver also defines several additional endpoints listed below. Please note that most of the driver-specific functionality is available using Execute Methods instead.

All endpoints listed below are supported since driver version 2.12.2, unless otherwise specified.

docs.title: availableIMEEngines
docs.text:
GET /session/:sessionId/ime/available_engines

JSONWP documentation: /session/:sessionId/ime/available_engines

Retrieves all IME (input method editor) engines available on the device under test.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string[] - a list of available IME engines

docs.title: getActiveIMEEngine
docs.text:
GET /session/:sessionId/ime/active_engine

JSONWP documentation: /session/:sessionId/ime/active_engine

Retrieves the name of the active IME engine.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - the name of the active IME engine

docs.title: isIMEActivated
docs.text:
GET /session/:sessionId/ime/activated

JSONWP documentation: /session/:sessionId/ime/activated

Determines if IME input is available and active.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if IME is active, otherwise false

docs.title: deactivateIMEEngine
docs.text:
POST /session/:sessionId/ime/deactivate

JSONWP documentation: /session/:sessionId/ime/deactivate

Deactivates the currently active IME engine.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: activateIMEEngine
docs.text:
POST /session/:sessionId/ime/activate

JSONWP documentation: /session/:sessionId/ime/activate

Activates an IME engine.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description engine string Name of the IME engine to activate

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: getWindowSize

docs.title: startRecordingScreen
docs.text:
POST /session/:sessionId/appium/start_recording_screen

Starts recording the device screen using Android's screenrecord tool. On emulators this functionality is only supported starting from Android 8 (Oreo / API level 27). The recording can be stopped either using the stopRecordingScreen endpoint, or by stopping the session itself.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Description options? Record<string, any> Options for starting the screen recording

The following keys are supported:

Name Type Description videoSize? string Dimensions of the resulting video, formatted as <width>x<height>. By default, the device's native display resolution is used, or 1280x720 if the native resolution is unsupported. For best results, use a size supported by your device's AVC encoder. bugReport? boolean Whether to add a video overlay with debugging information, such as a timestamp. Only supported since Android 9 (Pie / API level 28). timeLimit? float or string Maximum recording time in seconds. Set to 180 (3 minutes) by default. The maximum supported value is 1800 seconds (30 minutes). A single recording chunk can be at most 180 seconds long, so if a greater value is specified, the driver will attempt to use multiple chunks and combine them using ffmpeg. In such cases, if ffmpeg is not available on PATH, only the most recent chunk will be retained. bitRate? integer or string Bitrate of the video, in bits per second. Set to 20000000 (20Mbps) by default. forceRestart? boolean Whether to skip returning the results of any currently running screenrecording process, and start a new one right away

If forceRestart is false or unset (the default value), all the keys supported by the stopRecordingScreen endpoint can also be used, in order to handle the upload of the result from the currently running screenrecord process.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - the Base64-encoded string of a previous screen recording, if one existed and forceRestart and remotePath were not set, otherwise an empty string

docs.title: stopRecordingScreen
docs.text:
POST /session/:sessionId/appium/stop_recording_screen

Stops the active screen recording process started by startRecordingScreen, either returning its payload or uploading it to a remote location. On emulators this functionality is only supported starting from Android 9 (Pie / API level 28).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Description options? Record<string, any> Options for stopping the screen recording

The following keys are supported:

Name Type Description remotePath? string Path to a remote location where the resulting video file should be uploaded. Supported path protocols are HTTP(S) and FTP (deprecated). An exception is thrown if the file is too big to fit in the process memory. user? string Username used for authentication to remotePath pass? string Password used for authentication to remotePath method? string Name of the HTTP(S) multipart upload method. Set to PUT by default. headers? Record<string, any> Additional headers to use for the HTTP(S) multipart upload fileFieldName? string Name of the form field for storing the file content blob for HTTP(S) uploads. Set to file by default. formFields? Record<string, any> or Array<[string, any]> Additional form fields to use for the HTTP(S) multipart upload

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - the Base64-encoded string of the screen recording, or an empty string if remotePath is set or no active screen recording process is found

docs.title: Execute Methods
docs.text:
The UiAutomator2 driver provides various custom execute methods based on the standard Execute Script endpoint. Use the following examples in order to invoke them from your client code:

JavaJS (WebdriverIO)PythonRubyC# 
var result = driver.executeScript("mobile: <methodName>", Map.ofEntries(
    Map.entry("arg1", "value1"),
    Map.entry("arg2", "value2")
    // you may add more pairs if needed or skip providing the map completely
    // if all arguments are defined as optional
));

const result = await driver.executeScript('mobile: <methodName>', [{
    arg1: "value1",
    arg2: "value2",
}]);

result = driver.execute_script('mobile: <methodName>', {
    'arg1': 'value1',
    'arg2': 'value2',
})

result = @driver.execute_script 'mobile: <methodName>', {
    arg1: 'value1',
    arg2: 'value2',
}

object result = driver.ExecuteScript("mobile: <methodName>", new Dictionary<string, object>() {
    {"arg1", "value1"},
    {"arg2", "value2"}
}));

docs.title: mobile: scheduleAction
docs.text:
Adds a new action to the list of scheduled actions. Refer to the Scheduled Actions guide for more details.

Available since driver version 2.29.6.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Description name string Unique name of the action steps Array<ActionStep> One or more action steps to execute. See below for a detailed structure. Steps are executed in sequential order. All steps are executed even if any of them fails. The execution is considered failed if at least one step fails. maxPass? integer Number of successful action invocations after which it should automatically stop repeating maxFail? integer Number of unsuccessful action invocations after which it should automatically stop repeating times? integer Number of times the action should execute within a single invocation. Set to 1 by default intervalMs? integer Interval in milliseconds between subsequent action invocations. Set to 1000 by default maxHistoryItems? integer Maximum number of action invocation entries stored in history. All entries are sorted in descending order by action execution timestamp. If the number of entries exceeds this value, the oldest entry is deleted. Setting this parameter to a large value may cause out of memory issues. Set to 20 by default.

Each item in the steps array (ActionStep) must be an object with the following properties:

Name Type Description type string Type of the step. Supported values are gesture, source, and screenshot. name string Name of the step. Does not need to be unique. payload ActionStepPayload Payload of the step. See below for a detailed structure.

The contents of payload (ActionStepPayload) must be an object, and its properties depend on the value of type:

gesturesourcescreenshot

The object properties generally matches the property set for mobile: clickGesture, mobile: doubleClickGesture, or mobile: longClickGesture.

Name Type Description subtype string Can be set to click, longClick or doubleClick elementId? string Element to use as the click origin x? float X offset from the element origin or screen y? float Y offset from the element origin or screen locator? Record<string, string> Object with the strategy and selector keys. Useful for clicking dynamic elements duration? float Click duration (only for longClick subtype) Name Type Description subtype string Must be set to xml Name Type Description subtype string Must be set to png

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: getActionHistory
docs.text:
Returns the execution history for an action. Refer to the Scheduled Actions guide for more details.

Available since driver version 2.29.6.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description name string Name of the action to retrieve history for

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
ActionHistory - an object with the following properties:

Name Type Description repeats integer Number of times this action has been repeated so far stepResults Array<ActionInvocation> List of recorded action invocations, sorted by execution timestamp in descending order. See below for a detailed structure. The maximum length of the list is limited by maxHistoryItems.

Each item in stepResults array (ActionInvocation) is itself an array of objects, where each object has the following properties:

Name Type Description name string Name of the step as per its original ActionStep type string Type of step as per its original ActionStep timestamp integer Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the step execution start time passed boolean Whether the step passed result any Result of the step. Depends on the step type and subtype, and can be null. Always null if passed is false. exception Record<string, string> or null Object with the name, message and stacktrace properties of the raised exception. Always null if passed is true.
