docs.text: Executes the specified adb shell command on the device under test. The adb_shell insecure feature must be enabled.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description command string Shell command name to execute args? Array<string> Additional arguments to pass to the command. Keys and values should be provided as separate strings. timeout? integer Command timeout in milliseconds. An error is thrown if the command blocks for longer than this timeout. Set to 20000 by default includeStderr? boolean Whether to include stderr stream into the returned result. Set to false by default

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
string or Record<string, string> - contents of the returned stdout, or if includeStderr is true, an object with the stdout and stderr keys and their respective values.

An error is thrown if the command exits with a non-zero return code, with the error message matching the command's stderr.

docs.title: mobile: deviceInfo
docs.text: Retrieves information about the device under test.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Record<string, any> - mapping of device properties to their values. The following properties are included:

Name Description androidId Device identifier (ANDROID_ID) manufacturer Device manufacturer (MANUFACTURER) model Device model (MODEL) brand Device brand (BRAND) apiVersion Major Android version (VERSION.SDK_INT) platformVersion User-visible platform version (VERSION.RELEASE) carrierName Network carrier name (TelephonyManager.getNetworkOperatorName()) realDisplaySize Real size of the default display, in <width>x<height> format (based on Display.getRealSize()) displayDensity Display density in Density Independent Pixel units (based on DisplayMetrics.density) networks Array of objects, where each object contains information related to an available network type (based on ConnectivityManager.getAllNetworks(), ConnectivityManager.getNetworkInfo(network), and ConnectivityManager.getNetworkCapabilities(network)) locale System locale (Locale.getDefault()) timeZone System timezone (TimeZone.getDefault()) bluetooth Object with Bluetooth-related information, such as its state (BluetoothAdapter.getState())

docs.title: mobile: batteryInfo
docs.text: Retrieves battery-related information for the device under test.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Record<string, any> - object with battery-related information, with the following properties:

Name Type Description level float Current battery level fraction in range [0..1], where 1.0 means 100% charge. Set to -1 if the actual value cannot be retrieved from the system. (BatteryManager.EXTRA_LEVEL and BatteryManager.EXTRA_SCALE) state integer Current battery state, matching the value of a supported BATTERY_STATUS constant of the BatteryManager class. Set to -1 if the actual value cannot be retrieved from the system. (BatteryManager.EXTRA_STATE)

docs.title: mobile: getDeclaredOrientation
docs.text:
Retrieves the manifest-declared screen orientation of the current foreground activity (ActivityInfo.screenOrientation).

This reflects the value set in the activity's AndroidManifest.xml file (android:screenOrientation), which may differ from any runtime orientation overrides (e.g. Activity.setRequestedOrientation()) or the current display orientation (PORTRAIT/LANDSCAPE) returned by the Get Orientation API.

Available since driver version 8.5.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string | null - the name of the declared screen orientation constant (e.g. SCREEN_ORIENTATION_PORTRAIT), or null if the current activity is unknown or its manifest orientation cannot be resolved

docs.title: mobile: listDisplays
docs.text:
Retrieves a list of all displays available on the device under test. Under the hood, calls DisplayManager.getDisplays() for physical displays, and adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --displays for virtual displays.

Refer to the Multi-Window Testing guide for detailed usage information.

Available since driver version 6.6.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Array<Record<string, any>> - list of display information objects, where each object contains the following properties:

Name Type Description id integer Logical identifier of the display. Used by the currentDisplayId setting. name string or null Name of the display physicalId string or null Physical identifier of the display. Returned as a string to avoid JavaScript number precision issues with large values. Can be used by the mobile: screenshots method. virtualId string or null Virtual identifier of the display. Only set for virtual displays. Can be used by the mobile: screenshots method. metrics DisplayMetrics Display metrics such as size and density. See below for a detailed structure. isDefault boolean Whether this is the default display

The metrics item (DisplayMetrics) is an object with the following properties:

Name Type Description widthPixels integer Display width in pixels heightPixels integer Display height in pixels density float Display density (logical density factor). This is the scaling factor for the display. densityDpi integer Display density in DPI (dots per inch) scaledDensity float Scaled density factor for fonts. Usually the same as density, but may be adjusted by the user's font size preference. xdpi integer Exact physical pixels per inch of the screen in the X dimension ydpi integer Exact physical pixels per inch of the screen in the Y dimension

docs.title: mobile: listWindows
docs.text:
Retrieves a list of all windows on the device under test.

For devices running Android 11 (R / API level 30) or newer, this method retrieves all windows on all available displays (using UiAutomation.getWindowsOnAllDisplays()). For older devices, only windows from the default display are retrieved (using UiAutomation.getWindows()).

Refer to the Multi-Window Testing guide for detailed usage information.

Available since driver version 6.5.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Description filters? WindowFilters Conditions for filtering the returned list of windows. Specified conditions are applied using AND logic (all must match). See below for a detailed structure. skipScreenshots? boolean Whether to skip taking screenshots for each window. Screenshots are only supported since Android 14 (U / API level 34). Set to false by default. Setting this to true can improve performance.

The filters property (WindowFilters) is an object with the following properties:

Name Type Description packageName? string Name of the application package which the window should belong to. Can be specified as a glob pattern. windowId? integer Window identifier displayId? integer Logical display identifier physicalDisplayId? string Physical display identifier type? integer Window type, matching the value of a supported AccessibilityWindowInfo TYPE_ constant title? string Window title. Can be specified as a glob pattern. layer? number Z-order layer value of the window isAccessibilityFocused? boolean Whether the window has accessibility focus isActive? boolean Whether the window is active isFocused? boolean Whether the window has input focus isInPictureInPictureMode? boolean Whether the window is in picture-in-picture mode

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Array<Record<string, any>> - list of window information objects, where each object contains the following properties:

Name Type Description windowId integer or null Identifier of the window. Set to null if the identifier cannot be determined. displayId integer Logical identifier of the display that owns this window physicalDisplayId string or null Physical identifier of the display that owns this window. Returned as a string to avoid JavaScript number precision issues with large values. virtualDisplayId string or null Virtual identifier of the display that owns this window. Only set for virtual displays. rect Record<string, integer> Object with window bounds, containing the left, top, right, bottom properties packageName string Name of the application package which the window belongs to screenshot string or null Base64-encoded PNG screenshot of the window. Only supported since Android 14 (U / API level 34) if skipScreenshots is set to false. type integer Window type, matching the value of a supported AccessibilityWindowInfo TYPE_ constant title string or null Window title layer number Z-order layer value of the window isAccessibilityFocused boolean Whether the window has accessibility focus isActive boolean Whether the window is active isFocused boolean Whether the window has input focus isInPictureInPictureMode boolean Whether the window is in picture-in-picture mode

docs.title: mobile: viewportRect
docs.text: Retrieves the viewport bounds of the current window. This is equivalent to calling the standard Get Window Rect endpoint and subtracting the dimensions of the device status and navigation bars.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Record<string, integer> - an object with the following properties:

Name Type Description left integer X-axis offset of the viewport top integer Y-axis offset of the viewport width integer Viewport width height integer Viewport height

docs.title: mobile: getDisplayDensity
docs.text:
Retrieves the density of the current display in DPI.

Available since driver version 2.21.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: integer - the display density in DPI

docs.title: mobile: getSystemBars
docs.text:
Retrieves properties of various bars in the system UI.

Available since driver version 2.21.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Record<string, Record<string, any>> - mapping of system bar names to their properties. The following system bar names are included:

  • statusBar
  • navigationBar

All system bars include the following properties:

Name Type Description visible boolean Whether the bar is visible x integer Left X coordinate of the bar. Could be 0 if the bar is not visible y integer Top Y coordinate of the bar. Could be 0 if the bar is not visible width integer Bar width. Could be 0 if the bar is not visible height integer Bar height. Could be 0 if the bar is not visible

docs.title: mobile: getPerformanceData
docs.text:
Retrieves performance data about the given Android subsystem. The data is parsed from the output of the dumpsys utility.

Available since driver version 2.24.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description packageName string Name of the package identifier to fetch the data for dataType string Subsystem name to return the data for. Supported values can be retrieved using the mobile: getPerformanceDataTypes method.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Array<Array<any>[]> - table formatted as an array of arrays, where the first subarray represents column names, and the following subarrays represent data for those columns. The returned columns and their data depend on the specified dataType.

For example, a response for the cpuinfo datatype could look as follows: 

[
  [user, kernel],
  [0.9, 1.3]
]

docs.title: mobile: getPerformanceDataTypes
docs.text:
Retrieves supported performance data types, which can be used as the dataType argument for the mobile: getPerformanceData method.

Available since driver version 2.24.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Array<string> - list of supported data types

docs.title: mobile: startLogsBroadcast
docs.text:
Starts a websocket server for broadcasting Android logcat logs, using the host and port of the Appium server. The resulting endpoint is /ws/session/:sessionId:/appium/logcat. Broadcasting can be stopped using the mobile: stopLogsBroadcast execute method.

The method will return immediately if the web socket is already listening. Each listener will receive logcat log lines as soon as they are visible to Appium.

Refer to Using Mobile Execution Commands to Continuously Stream Device Logs with Appium for more details.

Consider using log broadcast via BiDi over this extension.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: stopLogsBroadcast
docs.text:
Stops the logcat websocket server previously started using mobile: startLogsBroadcast. The method will return immediately if no websocket server is running.

Refer to Using Mobile Execution Commands to Continuously Stream Device Logs with Appium for more details.

Consider using log broadcast via BiDi over this extension.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: resetAccessibilityCache
docs.text:
Resets the accessibility cache on the device under test. This method can be useful if the cache becomes stale and needs to be refreshed in order to reflect the current UI state.

The driver automatically resets this cache before any element lookup, as well as before retrieving the page source, but in case the application under test has highly dynamic elements, it may be beneficial to explicitly call this method, in order to avoid stale reference errors or interaction issues.

Note that this method also waits until the app under test becomes idle, so it may affect test performance if called too often under dynamic circumstances.

Available since driver version 6.4.1.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: getUiMode
docs.text:
Retrieves the value for the specified device appearance mode. Only supported since Android 10 (Q / API level 29). Calls adb shell cmd uimode under the hood.

Available since driver version 2.34.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description mode string Appearance mode to check. Supported values are night and car.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - value of the specified appearance mode

docs.title: mobile: setUiMode
docs.text:
Sets the device appearance mode. Only supported since Android 10 (Q / API level 29). Calls adb shell cmd uimode under the hood.

Available since driver version 2.34.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description mode string Appearance mode to set. Supported values are night and car. value string Value of the specified mode. Supported values are either yes, no, auto, custom_schedule, and custom_bedtime (for night mode), or yes and no (for car mode).

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: screenshots
docs.text:
Retrieves a screenshot of all device displays. Only supported since Android 10 (Q / API level 29).

This method uses physical or virtual display IDs, which are different from logical display IDs used by the currentDisplayId setting. Physical/virtual display IDs can be obtained using the mobile: listDisplays or mobile: listWindows execute methods, or the adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --display-id command.

Available since driver version 2.29.0. Virtual display IDs are supported since driver version 6.6.2.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description displayId? integer or string Physical or virtual display identifier to take a screenshot for. By default, all available displays are used. An error is thrown if a display with the specified ID does not exist.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Record<string, Record<string, any>> - a map of display identifiers to their properties. Each set of properties contains the following:

Name Type Description id string Display identifier name string Display name isDefault boolean Whether this display is the default one payload string Base64-encoded PNG screenshot of the display

docs.title: mobile: viewportScreenshot
docs.text: Retrieves a screenshot of the current viewport. This is equivalent to calling the standard Get Screenshot endpoint and cropping it to the visible viewport (returned by mobile: viewportRect).

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - a base64-encoded PNG image of the current viewport

docs.title: mobile: startScreenStreaming
docs.text:
Starts an MJPEG server for broadcasting the screen of the device under test. The adb_screen_streaming insecure feature must be enabled, and the host machine must have GStreamer installed and available on PATH, along with the gst-plugins-base, gst-plugins-good, gst-plugins-bad and gst-libav packages.

Broadcasting can be stopped using the mobile: stopScreenStreaming execute method. Repeated calls to this method have no effect unless the previous streaming session is stopped.

For the built-in device MJPEG stream (no GStreamer), see the MJPEG guide.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description width? integer Scaled width of the device screen. Set to the actual device screen width by default. height? integer Scaled height of the device screen. Set to the actual device screen height by default. bitRate? integer Bitrate of the video, in bits per second. Set to 4000000 (4 Mbps) by default. host? string IP address/host name to start the MJPEG server on. Set to 127.0.0.1 by default. Can be set to 0.0.0.0 to broadcast on all available network interfaces. pathname? string URL path on which the MJPEG server should be accessible. By default, all pathnames on the given host/port combination are accessible. Must begin with a forward slash (/). port? integer Port number to start the MJPEG server on. Set to 8093 by default. tcpPort? integer Port number to start the internal TCP MJPEG broadcast on. Always starts on the loopback interface (127.0.0.1). Set to 8094 by default. quality? integer Quality of the broadcasted images. Must be in the range [1, 100], where 100 indicates the best quality. Set to 70 by default. considerRotation? boolean Whether to increase the broadcast dimensions to fit both landscape and portrait orientations. Should be set to true if the device orientation will be changed during the broadcast. Set to false by default. logPipelineDetails? boolean Whether to include GStreamer pipeline event logs into the standard log output. Can be useful for debugging purposes. Set to false by default.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: stopScreenStreaming
docs.text:
Stops the MJPEG screen broadcasting server previously started using mobile: startScreenStreaming. The method will return immediately if no streaming server is running.

For the built-in device MJPEG stream (no GStreamer), see the MJPEG guide.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: startMediaProjectionRecording
docs.text:
Starts recording the device screen and audio using Android's Media Projection API. Only supported since Android 10 (Q / API level 29). Recording can be stopped using the mobile: stopMediaProjectionRecording execute method.

Available since driver version 2.4.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description resolution? string Resolution of the resulting video, formatted as <width>x<height>. Supported values are 1920x1080, 1280x720, 720x480, 320x240 and 176x144. Set to the greatest supported device resolution by default (usually 1920x1080). priority? string Priority of the recorder process, which could be adjusted in case of performance drops. Supported values are high, normal and low. Set to high by default. maxDurationSec? integer Maximum recording time in seconds. Set to 900 (15 minutes) by default. filename? string Name of the resulting video file. The .mp4 extension is added automatically if absent. Set to the current timestamp by default.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if a new recording has successfully started, otherwise false

docs.title: mobile: stopMediaProjectionRecording
docs.text:
Stops the active screen recording process started by mobile: startMediaProjectionRecording, either returning its payload or uploading it to a remote location. Only supported since Android 10 (Q / API level 29).

If the recording process is not running, but another recording has previously finished, its data is used instead. If no previous recording was found, an error is thrown.

Available since driver version 2.4.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description remotePath? string Path to a remote location where the resulting video file should be uploaded. Supported path protocols are HTTP(S) and FTP (deprecated). An exception is thrown if the file is too big to fit in the process memory. user? string Username used for authentication to remotePath pass? string Password used for authentication to remotePath method? string Name of the HTTP(S) multipart upload method. Set to PUT by default. headers? Record<string, any> Additional headers to use for the HTTP(S) multipart upload fileFieldName? string Name of the form field for storing the file content blob for HTTP(S) uploads. Set to file by default. formFields? Record<string, any> or Array<[string, any]> Additional form fields to use for the HTTP(S) multipart upload uploadTimeout? integer Maximum timeout for uploading the file. Set to 240000 (4 minutes) by default. Available since driver version 2.18.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - the Base64-encoded string of the screen recording, or an empty string if remotePath is set

docs.title: mobile: isMediaProjectionRecordingRunning
docs.text:
Determines whether a Media Projection-based recording is currently active. Only supported since Android 10 (Q / API level 29).

Available since driver version 2.4.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if recording is active, otherwise false

docs.title: mobile: lock
docs.text:
Locks the device and optionally unlocks it after a specified duration. Only simple (e.g. without a password) locks are supported.

Available since driver version 2.26.3.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description seconds? float Number of seconds after which to unlock the device. If omitted or set to 0, automatic unlock is skipped.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: unlock
docs.text: Unlocks the device if it is locked. Refer to the Device Lock/Unlock guide for more details.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description key? string The unlock key. By default, set to the value of the appium:unlockKey capability. Must be provided together with type. type? string The unlock type. By default, set to the value of the appium:unlockType capability. Supported values are pin, pinWithKeyEvent, password, pattern and fingerprint. Must be provided together with key. strategy? string Approach to use for unlocking. By default, set to the value of the appium:unlockStrategy capability. Ignored if type is set to fingerprint. timeoutMs? integer The unlock timeout. By default, set to the value of the appium:unlockSuccessTimeout capability.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: isLocked
docs.text:
Determines whether the device is locked.

Available since driver version 2.18.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if the device is locked, otherwise false

docs.title: mobile: getDeviceTime
docs.text: Retrieves the current system time on the device under test.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description format? string Format to return the timestamp in. Refer to the dayjs documentation for the format syntax. Set to YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ by default, matching the ISO8601 format.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - the device timestamp in the specified format

docs.title: mobile: openNotifications
docs.text:
Opens the notification tray on the device under test. Does nothing if the tray is already opened.

Available since driver version 2.23.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: getNotifications
docs.text:
Retrieves up to 100 most recent Android notifications, including dismissed ones.

For devices running Android 8 (Oreo / API level 27) or earlier, the Appium Settings helper app must first be manually granted notification access.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Record<string, any> - mapping of notification categories to arrays of notification objects. Newer notifications are always added to the start of the array. For details on the notification object, refer to the Android StatusBarNotification and Notification documentation. The isRemoved flag is set to true for dismissed notifications.

Example output:

{

    {

        "title": null,
        "bigTitle": "Appium Settings",
        "text": null,
        "bigText": "Keep this service running, so Appium for Android can properly interact with several system APIs",
        "tickerText": null,
        "subText": null,
        "infoText": null,
        "template": "android.app.Notification$BigTextStyle"
      },
      "userHandle": 0,
      "groupKey": "0|io.appium.settings|1|null|10133",
      "overrideGroupKey": null,
      "postTime": 1576853518850,
      "key": "0|io.appium.settings|1|null|10133",
      "isRemoved": false
    }

}

docs.title: mobile: statusBar
docs.text:
Performs the specified command on the system status bar. Calls adb shell cmd statusbar under the hood. Only supported since Android 8 (Oreo / API level 26).

Available since driver version 2.25.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Description command string Name of the status bar command. See below for supported values. component? string Name of the tile component to apply the command on. Only used for addTile, removeTile and clickTile commands.

The following values are supported for the command parameter:

Name Description expandNotifications Opens the notifications panel expandSettings Opens the notifications panel and expand quick settings if present collapse Collapses the notifications and settings panel addTile Adds a TileService of the specified component removeTile Removes a TileService of the specified component clickTile Clicks on a TileService of the specified component getStatusIcons Returns the list of status bar icons and the order they appear in. List items are separated using the newline character

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - output of the requested status bar command. Could be empty

docs.title: mobile: getConnectivity
docs.text:
Retrieves the state of one or more connectivity-related system services.

Available since driver version 2.13.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description services? string or Array<string> One or more service names to check. Supported values are wifi, data, and airplaneMode. By default, the states for all services are returned.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Record<string, boolean> - mapping of service names to whether they are enabled. If the services parameter was set, only the specified services are returned.

docs.title: mobile: setConnectivity
docs.text:
Sets the state of one or more connectivity-related system services. On real devices, switching WiFi only works reliably since Android 11 (R / API level 30).

Available since driver version 2.13.0.

Warning

Using this method may result in Android terminating/disconnecting the UiAutomator2 server app on the device under test, causing a session disconnect. The only way to restore the session afterwards would be to quit it, restore device connectivity, then reconnect to it with the appium:noReset capability set to true.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
At least one of the below parameters must be provided. If any parameter is not specified, the state of its service remains unchanged.

Name Type Description wifi? boolean Whether WiFi should be enabled or disabled data? boolean Whether mobile data should be enabled or disabled airplaneMode? boolean Whether Airplane Mode should be enabled or disabled

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: bluetooth
docs.text:
Performs the specified action on the Android system Bluetooth adapter. An error is thrown if the device under test does not have a Bluetooth adapter.

Available since driver version 3.4.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description action string Bluetooth action to apply. Supported values are enable, disable, and unpairAll.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: nfc
docs.text:
Performs the specified action on the Android system NFC adapter. An error is thrown if the device under test does not have a NFC adapter.

Available since driver version 3.4.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description action string NFC action to apply. Supported values are enable and disable.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: toggleGps
docs.text:
Toggles the state of location services (GPS). This functionality only works reliably starting from Android 12 (S / API level 31).

Available since driver version 2.23.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: isGpsEnabled
docs.text:
Determines whether location services (GPS) are enabled. This functionality only works reliably starting from Android 12 (S / API level 31).

Available since driver version 2.23.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if GPS services are enabled, otherwise false

docs.title: mobile: refreshGpsCache
docs.text:
Sends a request to refresh the GPS cache on the device under test. By default, location tracking is configured for low battery consumption, so this method can be useful if the device location frequently changes.

The device under test must either have Google Play Services installed, or be running Android 11 (R / API level 30) or later (which relies on LocationManager).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description timeoutMs? integer Maximum number of milliseconds to block until the GPS cache is confirmed to have been refreshed. Set to 20000 by default. An error is thrown if the device does not return a successful cache refresh response within this timeout. If set to 0 or a negative value, waiting is skipped.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: getGeolocation
docs.text:
Retrieves the current location of the device under test.

Available since driver version 3.8.1.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Location - an object with the following properties:

Name Type Description altitude float Altitude of the device location latitude float Latitude of the device location longitude float Longitude of the device location

docs.title: mobile: setGeolocation
docs.text:
Sets the current location of the device under test.

Available since driver version 3.8.1.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description latitude float New latitude value longitude float New longitude value altitude? float New altitude value satellites? integer Number of satellites being tracked. Only supported on emulators. Must be in the range [1, 12]. Available since driver version 4.1.0. speed? float Current speed in meters per second. Must not be negative. See Location.setSpeed for more details. Available since driver version 4.1.0. bearing? float Current bearing in degrees. Only supported on real devices. Must be in the range [0, 360). See Location.setBearing for more details. Available since driver version 4.1.0. accuracy? float Current horizontal accuracy in meters. Only supported on real devices. Must not be negative. See Location.setAccuracy for more details. Available since driver version 4.1.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: resetGeolocation
docs.text:
Resets the current location of the device under test to the default/system one. Only supported on real devices.

Available since driver version 3.8.1.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: pushFile
docs.text:
Pushes data to a file on the device under test. If the target file already exists, its contents will be overwritten.

Available since driver version 2.6.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description remotePath string Full path to the file where the data should be written to, or a path inside an app bundle (e.g. @my.app.id/my/path). The latter format requires the target app bundle to have debugging enabled. An error is thrown if the path resolves to a directory. payload string Base64-encoded data to be included in the file

docs.text:
Pulls the contents of a file from the device under test.

The latter format requires the target app bundle to have debugging enabled. An error is thrown if the path resolves to a directory.

docs.title: mobile: deleteFile

docs.title: Response

docs.title: mobile: pullFolder
docs.text:
Pulls the contents of a directory from the device under test.

docs.title: Parameters

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - Base64-encoded zipped contents of the specified directory

docs.title: mobile: hideKeyboard
docs.text:
Hides the on-screen keyboard. An error is thrown if the keyboard cannot be hidden.

Available since driver version 2.25.1.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if the keyboard was successfully hidden, otherwise false

docs.title: mobile: isKeyboardShown
docs.text:
Determines whether the on-screen keyboard is shown.

Available since driver version 2.16.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if the keyboard is shown, otherwise false

docs.title: mobile: setStylusHandwriting
docs.text:
Enables or disables the Android system stylus handwriting input method. The set_stylus_handwriting insecure feature must be enabled.

This functionality can be used to hide a possible system popup titled 'Try out your stylus'. Refer to this ticket for more details.

Available since driver version 7.1.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description enabled boolean Whether to enable or disable the stylus handwriting feature

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: getClipboard
docs.text:
Retrieves the content of the primary clipboard on the device under test.

Available since driver version 3.7.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - the clipboard content as a Base64-encoded string. An empty string is returned if the clipboard contains no data.

docs.title: mobile: setClipboard
docs.text:
Sets the contents of the primary device clipboard. Calls ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip() under the hood.

Available since driver version 3.7.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description content string Base64-encoded payload to place in the clipboard. contentType? string The only supported and default value is plaintext. label? string Label to identify the payload. By default, set to the first 10 symbols of the plaintext data.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: pressKey
docs.text:
Emulates a single key press of the specified key. Uses either pressKey() or a new KeyEvent under the hood.

Available since driver version 2.17.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description keycode integer Code of the key to press. Must match the numerical value for a supported KeyEvent KEYCODE_ constant. metastate integer One or more meta keys that should be simultaneously pressed. Must match the combined numerical value for one or more supported KeyEvent META_ constants. flags integer Flags to apply during the press. Must match the combined numerical value for one or more supported KeyEvent FLAG_ constants. isLongPress? boolean Whether to emulate a long press. Set to false by default. source? integer Input device source. Must be set to the value of an InputDevice SOURCE_ constant, or an bitwise OR combination of multiple such values. Set to 257 (SOURCE_KEYBOARD) by default. Available since driver version 6.8.0.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: execEmuConsoleCommand
docs.text: Executes the specified command using the Android emulator telnet console interface. The emulator_console insecure feature must be enabled. Only supported on emulators.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description command string or Array<string> Command name to execute. See Android Emulator Console Guide for more details on available commands execTimeout? integer Timeout in milliseconds to wait for the server to reply to the given command. Set to 60000 by default connTimeout? integer Console connection timeout in milliseconds. Set to 5000 by default initTimeout? integer Telnet console initialization timeout in milliseconds (the time between the connection being established and the command prompt becoming available). Set to 5000 ms by default

docs.title: Response
docs.text: string - the command output. An error is thrown if command execution fails.

docs.title: mobile: injectEmulatorCameraImage
docs.text:
Sets the specified image as the output of the camera viewfinder. Only supported on emulators.

This functionality can be useful, for example, when testing QR code scanning functionality in the application under test.

Available since driver version 3.2.0.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
If this method is used on a newly created or resetted device, it is mandatory to provide a value (or an empty map to use its defaults) to the appium:injectedImageProperties capability, in order to prepare the emulator for image injection.

There is also a possibility to perform a manual configuration of the necessary preconditions. For that, replace the content of the Toren1BD.posters file located in $ANDROID_HOME/emulator/resources with the following text:

poster wall
size 2 2
position -0.807 0.320 5.316
rotation 0 -150 0
default poster.png

poster table
size 1 1
position 0 0 -1.5
rotation 0 0 0

After that, make sure to (re)start the emulator to pick up the changes. The values under poster table can also be customized for different image properties.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description payload string Base64-encoded .PNG image to set as the viewfinder output. Other image formats are not supported.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: sendSms
docs.text:
Emulates sending an SMS to the specified phone number. Only supported on emulators.

Available since driver version 2.22.0.

docs.title: Parameters

docs.title: mobile: installApp

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description appPath string Full path to a file on the host machine, or URL to a remote location. The app must have the .apk or .apks extension. checkVersion? boolean Whether to skip installation if an identical or newer app version is already installed. Unset by default. Applied before replace. Available since driver version 2.45.0. timeout? integer Number of milliseconds to wait until the app is installed. Set to 60000 by default, unless overridden using the appium:adbExecTimeout capability allowTestPackages? boolean Whether to allow installation of test packages. Set to false by default useSdcard? boolean Whether to install the app on the SD card instead of built-in storage. Set to false by default grantPermissions? boolean Whether to automatically grant all permissions defined in the application manifest after installation. Set to false by default. Only supported on Android 6 (Marshmallow / API level 23) or later. replace? boolean Whether to replace any already existing app installation. Set to true by default. If set to false and the app is already installed, an error is thrown. Applied after checkVersion. noIncremental? boolean Whether to disable incremental app installation. Set to false by default. Refer to How ADB incremental-install works for more details.

docs.title: mobile: installMultipleApks

Name Type Description allowTestPackages? boolean Whether to allow installation of test packages. Only supported on Android 6 (Marshmallow / API level 23) or later. replace? boolean Whether to replace any already existing app installations. Set to true by default. If set to false and any app is already installed, an error is thrown. partialInstall? boolean Whether to use partial application installs (i.e. non-standalone updates). docs.title: mobile: changePermissions
docs.text:

docs.title: Parameters

For pm mode, supported values can be found in the Android Manifest documentation, and the all magic string is additionally supported since driver version 2.8.0. For appops mode, supported values can be found in the Android AppOpsManager documentation. Full constant values must be used for both modes. appPackage? string Name of the application package to change. Set to the package of the app under test by default. action string Permission action to apply. Supported values are either grant or revoke (in pm mode), or allow, ignore, deny and default (in appops mode). target? string The mode to use. Supported values are pm and appops. docs.title: mobile: startActivity
docs.text: Starts the specified app activity using adb shell am start-activity.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Description intent? string Full name of the activity intent to start user? integer or string ID of the user to start the activity for. By default, the default user is used. wait? boolean Whether to block the call until the Activity Manager's process returns control to the system. Unset by default. stop? boolean Whether to stop the target app before starting the activity. Unset by default. windowingMode? integer Windowing mode to launch the activity intent into. Supported values can be found in the Android source code as WINDOWING_MODE_ constants. activityType? integer Activity type to launch the intent as. Supported values can be found in the Android source code as ACTIVITY_TYPE_ constants. action? string Intent action to apply when launching the app. Refer to the Android Intent documentation for a list of possible values (prefixed with ACTION_). uri? string Activity intent URI mimeType? string Activity intent MIME type identifier? string Activity intent identifier categories? string or Array<string> One or more activity intent categories. Refer to the Android Intent documentation for a list of possible values (prefixed with CATEGORY_). component? string Activity intent component package? string Activity intent package name display? integer or string Display identifier to launch the activity intent on extras? ActivityExtras Extra activity intent arguments. See below for expected structure flags? string Flags in hexadecimal format to apply on activity intent start-up. Refer to the Android Intent documentation for possible values (prefixed with FLAG_). Multiple flags should be combined into one value using bitwise OR.

The extras parameter (ActivityExtras) is an array of arrays, where each subarray contains 3 items: value category, key, and the value itself. Supported value categories and their value types are as follows:

Value Category Value Type s String sn Null (only the key is required; the value should be omitted) z Boolean i Integer l Long integer f Float u URI cn Component name (string) ia String of comma-separated integers ial String of comma-separated integers la String of comma-separated long integers lal String of comma-separated long integers fa String of comma-separated floats fal String of comma-separated floats sa Comma-separated strings (commas that are part of the strings themselves should be escaped) sal Comma-separated strings (commas that are part of the strings themselves should be escaped)

docs.text:

Unlike the standard Get Element Rect endpoint, this method adjusts the result depending on the visible viewport, zoom level, iframes, scroll offsets, ancestor frame offsets, webview bounds, and the device pixel ratio. An error is thrown if the element is fully located outside of the visible viewport.

Either this property or elementId must be provided. Ignored if both are provided. speed? integer Speed of the pinch gesture in pixels per second. Set to 1000 * displayDensity by default.

docs.title: mobile: pinchCloseGesture
docs.text: Performs a pinch close gesture on the specified element or area using the W3C Actions API.

Must be in range (0..1]. elementId? string The identifier of an element whose bounds should be used as the pinch area. Either this property or elementId must be provided. Ignored if both are provided. speed? integer Speed of the pinch gesture in pixels per second. Set to 1000 * displayDensity by default.

docs.title: mobile: scroll
docs.text:
Scrolls a scrollable view until the element identified by strategy and selector becomes visible. The scroll direction is detected automatically.

This function returns immediately if the destination element is already visible in the viewport.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description strategy string Locator strategy to use for finding the target element. The following values are supported: accessibility id, class name, and -android uiautomator. selector string Element selector to use for the specified locator strategy elementId? string Identifier of the view to scroll. The view matching this identifier must be a valid scrollable container located using the -android uiautomator strategy. By default, the first currently available scrollable view is used. maxSwipes? integer Maximum number of swipes to perform on the scrollable view in order to reach the destination element. By default, the value is retrieved from the scrollable element itself (getMaxSearchSwipes()).

docs.text: null

docs.title: mobile: scrollBackTo
docs.text: Scrolls a scrollable view until the target element becomes visible. The scroll direction is detected automatically.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description elementId string Identifier of the view to scroll. The view matching this identifier must be a valid scrollable container located using the -android uiautomator strategy. elementToId string Identifier of the element to scroll to. The element matching this identifier must be locatable using the -android uiautomator strategy.

docs.title: mobile: type
docs.text:
Types the given string in the currently focused input field element.

Unlike the standard Element Send Keys endpoint, this method emulates 'true' typing equivalent to an on-screen keyboard, and properly supports Unicode input characters.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description text string or float or boolean Text to type

docs.title: Response
docs.text: boolean - true if text was successfully sent to adb, otherwise false

docs.title: mobile: replaceElementValue
docs.text:
Sets the value of a given element, replacing its existing value.

Available since driver version 2.22.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description elementId string Identifier of the element to set the value of text string New text value of the element. Can contain Unicode characters. If the text ends with \\n (the backslash must be escaped, so that it is not translated into 0x0A), the Enter key press will be emulated instead.

docs.title: mobile: performEditorAction
docs.text:
Performs IME action on the currently focused editable element.

Very often Android developers use the onEditorAction callback with the actionId argument to implement handling of actions, for example, when the Search or Done button is pressed on the on-screen keyboard. This method aims to emulate the invocation of such a callback on the focused element.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description action integer or string Name or integer code of the editor action to be executed. Supported values are unspecified, none, go, search, send, next, done, and previous. Refer to the Android EditorInfo documentation for more details.
