docs.title: Insecure Features
docs.text:
Some insecure driver features are disabled by default. They can be enabled upon launching Appium as follows: 

appium --allow-insecure uiautomator2:<feature-name>
or 
appium --relaxed-security

For other insecure feature names recognized by the Appium server, see their Appium docs reference page.

docs.title: adb_listen_all_network
docs.text:
Allows enabling the underlying adb instance to listen on all network interfaces using the appium:adbListenAllNetwork capability.

Available since driver version 6.7.0.

docs.title: adb_screen_streaming
docs.text: Enables broadcasting the device screen over MJPEG using the mobile: startScreenStreaming execute method.

docs.title: adb_shell
docs.text: Enables shell-related functionality for the underlying adb instance. Can be used in execute methods like mobile: shell.

docs.title: chromedriver_autodownload
docs.text:
Enables automatic download of a ChromeDriver binary compatible with the active webview. Only relevant in a webview context.

Refer to the Hybrid Mode guide for more details.

docs.title: emulator_console
docs.text: Enables execution of Android emulator telnet console interface commands using the mobile: execEmuConsoleCommand execute method. Not relevant for real devices.

docs.title: get_server_logs
docs.text: Enables retrieval of Appium server logs using the getLogEvents endpoint and the log.entryAdded BiDi event.

docs.title: set_stylus_handwriting
docs.text:
Enables toggling the Android stylus handwriting feature using the mobile: setStylusHandwriting execute method.

Available since driver version 7.1.0.

docs.title: Locator Strategies
docs.text: The UiAutomator2 driver supports several location strategies in the native context. The list below describes each strategy along with usage recommendations.

docs.title: Id
docs.text:
Name Speed Ranking Example id ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ com.mycompany:id/resourceId

This strategy is mapped to the native UI Automator BySelector.res matcher, which returns elements whose resource name matches the specified value exactly.

If the package identifier prefix is not specified and the disableIdLocatorAutocompletion setting is not enabled, the prefix identifier of the current app under test is added automatically.

When to Use

Use this strategy for elements that can be identified using their View.id attribute value.

docs.title: Accessibility Id
docs.text:
Name Speed Ranking Example accessibility id ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ my description

This strategy is mapped to the native UI Automator BySelector.desc matcher, which returns elements whose content description matches the specified value exactly.

When to Use

Use this strategy for elements that can be identified using their View.contentDescription attribute value.

docs.title: Class Name
docs.text:
Name Speed Ranking Example class name ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ android.view.View

This strategy is mapped to the native UI Automator BySelector.clazz matcher, which returns elements whose class name matches the specified value exactly.

When to Use

Use this strategy for elements that can be identified using their class name.

docs.title: UiAutomator
docs.text:
Name Speed Ranking Example -android uiautomator ⭐⭐⭐⭐ new UiSelector().resourceId("android:id/list")

This strategy is mapped to the native UI Automator UiSelector locator.

The strategy also allows to implicitly perform some advanced operations, like scrolling. Refer to the UiAutomator Locator Strategy guide for more details.

Warning

Google is planning to deprecate and remove UiCollection, UiObject, UiScrollable, and UiSelector support from the UiAutomator framework. This will render all -android uiautomator-based locators invalid, so keep this in mind while using them or planning to use them in the future.

When to Use

Use this strategy for elements that cannot be directly identified by their class name, id, or contentDescription.

docs.title: XPath
docs.text:
Name Speed Ranking Example xpath ⭐⭐⭐ //android.view.View[@text="Regular" and @checkable="true"]

This strategy relies on the XML tree generated by the UiAutomator2 driver's page source API.

XPath versions 1.0 and 2.0 are supported.

When to Use

Use this strategy when no other strategy is applicable, typically for elements that can only be identified from their sibling or descendant elements.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
Appium drivers can include scripts for executing specific actions. The scripts included in the UiAutomator2 driver can be run as follows:

appium driver run uiautomator2 <script-name>

For more information about the appium driver run command, refer to the Appium docs.

docs.title: reset
docs.text:
Uninstalls all driver-related packages (UiAutomator2 Server and Appium Settings) from all connected devices. This can be useful after a driver update, if the packages installed on the test device(s) remain cached with their older versions.

Available since driver version 2.12.5.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: appium driver run uiautomator2 reset

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: The UiAutomator2 driver exposes various settings through Appium's Settings API.

docs.title: actionAcknowledgmentTimeout
docs.text:
Type Default long 3000

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait for an acknowledgment of a generic UI Automator click action. Calls Configurator.setActionAcknowledgmentTimeout() under the hood.

docs.title: allowInvisibleElements
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to include elements that are not visible to the user (whose displayed attribute is false) in the XML source tree.

docs.title: alwaysTraversableViewClasses
docs.text:
Type Default string ""

Comma separated list of Android element classes, whose visible/invisible state should be ignored by the UiAutomator2 server during the application source tree traversal.

The default logic for the UI tree traversal (controlled by the allowInvisibleElements setting) is to stop recursing when an invisible node is found. However, with certain Jetpack Compose classes (e.g. androidx.compose.ui.viewinterop.ViewFactoryHolder), invisible parent nodes may have visible child nodes. See this Google issue and this UiAutomator2 server issue for more details.

This setting only affects the XPath lookup and the page source buildup. The list of classes may also include glob patterns, e.g. androidx.compose.ui.viewinterop.*,android.widget.ImageButton.

Available since driver version 5.0.3.

docs.title: currentDisplayId
docs.text:
Type Default integer 0 (Display.DEFAULT_DISPLAY)

Identifier of the display that should be used for driver actions such as retrieving screenshot, finding elements, etc. Available values can be retrieved using the mobile: listDisplays execute method, or by running adb shell dumpsys display (search for mDisplayId).

If set to -1, the display is reset to the default one.

Refer to the Multi-Window Testing guide for detailed usage information.

Available since driver version 4.2.0.

docs.title: deferAccessibilityCacheReset
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether the UiAutomator2 server should clear the accessibility cache for element/source lookups only if a relevant UI-change AccessibilityEvent has been observed since the last reset. By default, the cache is cleared for every element/source lookup, which prevents the cache from going stale, but may result in significant memory usage under sustained lookups.

See this UiAutomator2 server issue for more details.

Available since driver version 8.1.0.

docs.title: disableIdLocatorAutocompletion
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to disable automatic prefixing of resource-id-based element selectors with the application package name.

Internal Android standards expect each element resource identifier to be prefixed with the <packageName>:id/ string. This is done to ensure uniqueness of each identifier. However, this rule is not strictly enforced, and different development frameworks either ignore this or leave this behavior up to the developer: for example, in Jetpack Compose, using the testTag modifier attribute with testTagsAsResourceId allows setting an arbitrary string without the prefix rule. Interoperability with UiAutomator also explains how to set it.

By default, the driver adds the above prefix automatically to all unprefixed resource-id locators, but this setting allows disabling this behavior.

Available since driver version 2.0.6.

docs.title: elementResponseAttributes
docs.text:
Type Default string name,text

Comma-separated list of element attribute names to be included into element search responses. The following values are supported: name, text, rect, enabled, displayed, selected, attribute/<element_attribute_name>.

Has no effect if the shouldUseCompactResponses setting is set to true.

docs.title: enableMultiWindows
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to include all windows that the user can interact with (e.g. an on-screen keyboard) while building the application page source. By default, only the focused active application window is included in the page source.

Refer to the Multi-Window Testing guide for detailed usage information.

docs.title: enableNotificationListener
docs.text:
Type Default boolean true

Whether to enable the listener for new toast notifications and allow toast message texts to be included into the application page source. By default, this listener is enabled and tracks toast messages for up to 3500 ms after their expiration.

docs.title: enableTopmostWindowFromActivePackage
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to select the application window with the highest Z-order as the active window. By default, the driver selects the focused window, which generally also has the highest Z-order, but this may not be the case for multi-window apps, or devices with multiple displays.

Refer to the Multi-Window Testing guide for detailed usage information.

Available since driver version 2.25.2.

docs.title: enforceXPath1
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to enforce usage of XPath1 for XPath-based element lookup.

The default built-in XPath2 interpreter is based on the PsychoPath implementation, which is identical to an XPath1 interpreter for most cases, but more sophisticated locators may run into issues due to different behavior. This setting can be used to try to workaround such issues by enforcing XPath1 usage (whose implementation is a part of the Android platform itself).

This setting is primarily relevant for driver versions 7.5.1 or earlier, since the issues that resulted in the introduction of this setting were solved in version 7.5.2, as a result of vendoring the PsychoPath library.

docs.title: ignoreUnimportantViews
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to enable compression of the application source layout hierarchy.

If enabled, the layout hierarchy derived from the accessibility framework will only contain nodes that are important for UI Automator testing. Any unnecessary surrounding layout nodes that make viewing and searching the hierarchy inefficient are removed.

docs.title: includeA11yActionsInPageSource
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to include the actions element attribute in the application source. This attribute value could be huge if elements in the page source have a lot of actions, which could affect the performance of page source generation.

Available since driver version 4.0.0.

docs.title: includeExtraRenderingInfo
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to include the text-size and text-unit element attributes in the application source. Retrieval of these attributes has a slight effect on the performance of page source generation.

Available since driver version 6.7.10.

docs.title: includeExtrasInPageSource
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to include the extras element attribute in the application source. This attribute value could be huge if elements in the page source have a lot of extras, which could affect the performance of page source generation.

Available since driver version 2.1.0.

docs.title: keyInjectionDelay
docs.text:
Type Default integer 0

Delay in milliseconds between key presses, used when inputting text.

docs.title: limitXPathContextScope
docs.text:
Type Default boolean true

Whether to limit the context scope of XPath-based element lookups to the parent element.

Due to historical reasons, by default, the driver limits the scope of element context-based searches to the parent element. This means that a request like findElement(By.xpath, "//root").findElement(By.xpath, "./..") would always fail, because the driver only collects descendants of the root element. Disabling this setting causes the retrieved page source to includes the entire page source, resulting in the aforementioned query to no longer fail.

Disabling this setting nonetheless requires caution with other context-based queries - for example, a request like findElement(By.xpath, "//root").findElement(By.xpath, "//element") would ignore the current context and search for element through the whole page source. In such cases it is recommended to use the dot (.) notation: findElement(By.xpath, "//root").findElement(By.xpath, ".//element").

Available since driver version 2.0.2.

docs.title: mapTestTagToResourceId
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to map the testTag semantic property of Jetpack Compose elements onto their resource-id attribute.

Enabling this setting mirrors the behavior of Compose's own testTagsAsResourceId, which can otherwise only be toggled from within the app's own composable tree. The mapping is consistently applied to element attribute retrieval, page source/XPath generation, and id-based element lookups. Unlike the disableIdLocatorAutocompletion setting, bare testTag values are matched as-is, without automatically prepending the application package name.

Available since driver version 8.4.0.

docs.title: mjpegBilinearFiltering
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to apply bilinear filtering to the MJPEG screenshot broadcaster's resize algorithm. Enabling this flag may improve the quality of the resulting scaled bitmap, but may introduce a small performance hit.

Refer to the MJPEG guide for more details.

docs.title: mjpegScalingFactor
docs.text:
Type Default integer 50

The percentage value to which the screenshots generated by the MJPEG screenshot broadcaster are downscaled. Must be in range 1..100. By default, screenshots are downscaled to half of their original size.

Refer to the MJPEG guide for more details.

docs.title: mjpegServerFramerate
docs.text:
Type Default integer 10

Maximum screenshots per second taken by the MJPEG screenshot broadcaster. Must be in range 1..60.

Refer to the MJPEG guide for more details.

docs.title: mjpegServerPort
docs.text:
Type Default integer 7810

The port on the device under test to start the MJPEG screenshot broadcaster on. Must be in range 1024..65535.

On the host machine, the forwarded MJPEG server port can be configured using the appium:mjpegServerPort capability.

Refer to the MJPEG guide for more details.

docs.title: mjpegServerScreenshotQuality
docs.text:
Type Default integer 50

The percentage value of the quality to which the screenshots generated by the MJPEG screenshot broadcaster are compressed. Must be in range 1..100. By default, screenshots are compressed to half of their original quality.

Refer to the MJPEG guide for more details.

docs.title: normalizeTagNames
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to apply Unicode-to-ASCII normalization of element class names, when converting them to XML tag names in the application page source. This setting can be useful if the application under test has some Unicode class names which cannot be used as XML tag names, due to known bugs in Android's XML DOM parser implementation.

docs.title: scrollAcknowledgmentTimeout
docs.text:
Type Default long 200

Maximum number of milliseconds to wait for an acknowledgment of a UiScrollable scroll action. Calls Configurator.setScrollAcknowledgmentTimeout() under the hood.

docs.title: serverPort
docs.text:
Type Default integer 6790

The port on the device under test to start the UiAutomator2 server on. Must be in range 1024..65535.

On the host machine, the forwarded UiAutomator2 server port can be configured using the appium:systemPort capability.

docs.title: shouldUseCompactResponses
docs.text:
Type Default boolean true

Whether to enable compact responses for element search requests. If disabled, responses will include the attributes specified by the elementResponseAttributes setting.

docs.title: shutdownOnPowerDisconnect
docs.text:
Type Default boolean true

Whether to shutdown the UiAutomator2 server if the device under test is disconnected from a power source and remains on battery power.

docs.title: simpleBoundsCalculation
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to calculate element bounds as absolute values, instead of always checking if the element may be covered by other elements and is therefore partially hidden.

Enabling this setting improves the performance of generating the application page source, but decreases precision of element bounds. Use with care.

docs.title: snapshotMaxDepth
docs.text:
Type Default integer 70

The maximum retrieved depth of the application page source tree. Lower values can help speed up source retrieval and prevent out of memory or timeout errors such as #12545 or #12892. Must be in range 1..500.

Available since driver version 2.27.0.

docs.title: trackScrollEvents
docs.text:
Type Default boolean true

Whether to track all scroll events for the purpose of calculating the value of elements' contentSize attribute. Disabling this setting may speed up all scrolling actions.

docs.title: useResourcesForOrientationDetection
docs.text:
Type Default boolean false

Whether to detect device orientation using Android's Configuration state, instead of calculating it from the device rotation state. This setting can be useful for certain devices where the default rotation approach does not work properly, and erroneously detects a portrait orientation as landscape (and vice versa).

docs.title: waitForIdleTimeout
docs.text:
Type Default long 10000

Maximum timeout in milliseconds to wait until the application user interface enters an idle state.

By default, the UiAutomator2 server performs this wait for all core UI Automator objects (except UiDevice) before searching for the element matching the object's locator. Reducing this value may help in mitigating long delays when interacting with elements.

docs.title: waitForSelectorTimeout
docs.text:
Type Default long 10000

Maximum timeout in milliseconds to wait for an element match, when searching using the -android uiautomator locator strategy.

Since content in the user interface is dynamic, sometimes an element may not be immediately visible, and will not be detected by a selector. This timeout adds an extra wait during search, until at least one match is found.

This setting only affects element searches using the -android uiautomator location strategy.

docs.title: wakeLockTimeout
docs.text:
Type Default long 86400000 (24 hours)

Maximum timeout in milliseconds for how long the UiAutomator2 server should prevent the device under test from going to sleep during an automated test.

Setting this value to zero forces the server to release the wake lock.

docs.title: Outdated Driver Binaries
docs.text:
Sometimes various older driver binaries (like Appium Settings) might be cached on the device under test, which would prevent a new/upgraded driver version from starting a session.

Run the built-in reset script in order to cleanup the cached binaries from all connected devices on the current machine.

docs.title: Permission Denial When Starting Intent
docs.text:
The full error description usually looks like 'java.lang.SecurityException: Permission Denial: starting Intent { act=android.intent.action.MAIN cat=[android.intent.category.LAUNCHER] flg=0x10200000 cmp=com.mypackage/.myactivity.MainActivity launchParam=MultiScreenLaunchParams { mDisplayId=0 mBaseDisplayId=0 mFlags=0 } } from null (pid=11366, uid=2000) not exported from uid 10191. An error like this might indicate that the provided application package and activity name (either passed to UiAutomator2 as appium:appPackage / appium:appActivity or auto detected), is not the correct one to start the application under test.

In order to fix this, it is necessary to check the correct values with the application developer, and test them manually first by executing: adb shell am start -W -n com.myfixedpackage/.myfixedactivity.MainActivity -S -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER -f 0x10200000. If this commands succeeds manually and starts the necessary application on the device, then it will work for the UiAutomator2 driver as well.

Some devices might also require adjustments to their the security configuration in the developer options, or security preferences. For example, Realme devices require Disable Permission Monitoring and a couple of flags in the developer options in order to avoid a Permission Denial error.

docs.title: Activity Never Started
docs.text:
This problem may manifest with a message like com.myactivity.* never started. It usually indicates that the first application activity (either passed to UiAutomator2 as appium:appWaitPackage / appium:appWaitActivity or auto-detected) is not the one actually launched as the first one. This problem typically occurs in applications with multiple activities.

In order to resolve the problem, one should check with application developer regarding which activity/package is the very first one that appears on application startup. The currently focused activity name can be verified using the adb shell dumpsys window windows command (see the Activity Startup guide).

The UiAutomator2 driver also allows the use of wildcards in the appium:appWaitActivity value, which can be particularly useful if the activity name is generated dynamically, or it is not the same all the time. For example, com.mycompany.* will match any of com.mycompany.foo, com.mycompany.bar.

docs.title: Command Timed Out
docs.text:
If the activity names are correct, but the startup still times out, another possible approach is to increase the value of the app:appWaitDuration capability. Normally, the default 20 seconds is enough for the most of applications, however, some bigger apps might require more time to start and show the first activity. (It is strongly recommended to not develop apps to behave this way.)

There may also be situations where the launch activity does not return the control to the calling process at all. This could be mitigated by setting the appium:autoLaunch capability to false, which skips waiting for the activity. However, by choosing this option, the driver cannot make sure the activity has fully started, so then it is up to the client code to verify the initial UI state is the one that is expected.

docs.title: Firebase Installations Exception
docs.text:
firebaseinstallations.googleapis.com sends the APK file's certificate information in the X-Android-Cert header in its initialization step. The UiAutomator2 driver re-signs the application under test with the default Appium debug signature. This may cause an exception (java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException: com.google.firebase.installations.FirebaseInstallationsException) when the application under test starts.

To avoid this problem, set the appium:noSign capability to true, which skips the re-signing process. For more details, refer to the Unblocking Firebase Network Traffic in Modified Android Applications guide.

docs.title: Session Deleted Due to Socket Hangup
docs.text: This type of error means the driver is unable to connect to the UiAutomator2 REST server running on the device under test. There might be multiple causes for this issue:

docs.title: Already Terminated by Script
docs.text:
Sending a Delete Session request terminates both the session and the UiAutomator2 server on the device. Any further commands sent to the same UiAutomator2 server would return a socket hangup error.

Such issues can happen if the test script does not properly configure session management, for example, by starting a new session while the previous one is still running and has not been quit properly, or there is a timeout while waiting for a new command. Adjusting the session management logic (e.g. making sure each session is being properly created in the test setup section and is terminated in the test teardown) or changing/disabling the command timeout (see the appium:newCommandTimeout capability) might help to address such errors.

docs.title: Terminated by Android OS
docs.text:
There may be situations where Android itself kills the session. The recommended approach here is to debug the problem by fetching the logcat output and finding occurrences of io.appium.uiautomator2.server traces labeled with error or exception.

Sometimes it may be necessary to turn off some internal phone optimizations, sometimes the server crashes because of an internal UI Automator framework bug, sometimes because of a bug in the server code itself. Each case should be investigated separately if the search over the internet shows no matches...

docs.title: Unstable Connection
docs.text: The connectivity between the phone and the host is unstable. Nothing much to add on this one. Maybe the phone has a defect, or the USB cable is damaged, or the installed Android SDK is out of date...

docs.title: Element(s) Cannot Be Found
docs.text:
All element location strategies in the UiAutomator2 driver work similarly under the hood, except for xpath. If some element is not found, but it is (or should be) present in the page source, the following may help:

  • Check that the selector does not contain any typos
  • Make sure there are no race conditions
  • Add a timeout of several seconds before stopping the element search

In case the lookup still fails while using a non-XPath locator, then it is likely that the target element is actually not present. There is not much that could be done in the driver to change/influence this, since such lookup calls are passed directly to Google's UI Automator framework. Still, the driver provides several settings that may help:

Warning

The default values for the following settings have been set for optimal element lookup and page source generation performance. Continuously using different values may sometimes significantly (especially in case of large app sources) reduce element lookup and page source generation speed.

docs.title: Common Settings
docs.text:
• allowInvisibleElements

    By default, this setting is set to false, which hides elements that are not visible from the page source and from the xpath location. Changing this value to true would add such invisible elements to the page source and make them locatable.

  • ignoreUnimportantViews

    This setting is enabled by default. By disabling it, the page source could receive more elements that are normally hidden due to their unimportance.

  • enableMultiWindows

    This setting, if set to true, extends the page source by adding the actual content of other windows that are currently present on the device's screen. For example, the on-screen keyboard in Android is not a part of the current app hierarchy, but rather belongs to a separate window.

  • snapshotMaxDepth

    For this setting, it only makes sense to change its default value if the application under test has deeply nested elements in the page tree hierarchy (e.g. more than 70 levels), and the destination element is suspected to be a part of these deeply nested views. Increasing the value of this setting will reduce the performance of XPath searches and page tree retrievals, so be careful while assigning too high values to it.

docs.title: Id Locators
docs.text:
The following settings may adjust the behavior of id-based locators:

  • disableIdLocatorAutocompletion

    The general resources naming convention for Android apps is <app_id>:id/<resource_name>. This should guarantee uniqueness of each identifier accross the user interface. However, this is only a convention, and Android still allows to have various resource names that do not follow this format. If testing an application like this, consider changing the disableIdLocatorAutocompletion setting to true, so that the driver does not automatically rewrite selector values by adding <app_id>:id/ prefixes to them.

  • mapTestTagToResourceId

    If testing a Jetpack Compose application, its elements may have the testTag semantic property. Changing this setting to true replaces the value of the retrieved resource-id attribute for such elements with the value their testTag property, which can then be used in id-based locators.

docs.title: XPath Locators
docs.text:
The following settings may adjust the behavior of xpath-based locators:

  • alwaysTraversableViewClasses

    This setting is similar to allowInvisibleElements, but primarily aimed at Jetpack Compose applications, which may contain invisible nodes with visible child elements. By default, such child elements are not included in the application source.

docs.title: ClassCastException During XPath Lookup
docs.text:
Driver versions older than 7.5.2 may encounter the following error for complex XPath2-based queries:

ClassCastException: java.util.ArrayList$ListItr cannot be cast to org.eclipse.wst.xml.xpath2.processor

This exception was caused by a bug in the Eclipse's PsychoPath library used by the driver to support XPath2 syntax. The issue was primarily observed while using following:: or preceding:: axes in XPath queries (e.g. (//android.widget.TextView[@text='some, text']/following::android.widget.ImageButton)[1]).

The bug has been fixed since driver version 7.5.2. For older driver versions, a possible workaround is to set the enforceXPath1 setting, which forcefully switches the driver's XPath processor to the standard Android's Apache Harmony-based XPath1, which does not have this issue (but also does not support XPath2 syntax). Refer to issue #16142 for more details.

docs.title: Slow Element Interaction
docs.text:
If tests need at least 10 seconds or more to locate/interact with a single element, consider changing the default value of the waitForIdleTimeout setting.

By default, the UI Automator framework (and all other Accessibility-based frameworks) always waits for the accessibility event stream to become idle before interacting with an element. This is needed to make sure all animations/transitions are finished before, for example, interacting with an element by clicking it. In case the application under test constantly runs some background animations or hogs the accessibility event stream in some other way, these waits may significantly slow down the automation flow.

Setting the value of waitForIdleTimeout to 0 should completely disable any waits, and enforce interactions to happen immediately ignoring the accessibility event stream state. The downside of that would be that all interactions are never going to be delayed, so clicks and other actions might happen at wrong places of the application UI. That is why is it important to check the app under test first and fix its source to get rid of activities hogging the event loop. Sometimes it makes sense to disable animations completely for the app build under test, which could speed up test flows significantly in some situations.

docs.title: Scroll/Swipe Gestures Have No Effect
docs.text:
The UiAutomator2 driver provides multiple options for automating touch gestures:

  • For simple gestures, like swipe, scroll, drag, double click, fling or pinch, use the supported gesture execute methods
  • Certain scrolling behaviors may also be automatable using UiScrollable-based UiAutomator locators
  • For more sophisticated gestures, consider using W3C actions

The deprecated JSONWP TouchActions API is no longer supported since driver version 3.0.0.

If the action code in the client source looks good and satisfies the above requirements, but its execution still does not deliver the expected result, then the following debugging meassures may help:

  • Enable Show taps and Pointer location Developer options in the device Settings. When running a test script with these options enabled, the device screen will show the exact pointer trace path, allowing to check the velocity of the gesture. This also works for multi-touch gestures. This trace can then be compared to a manual use of the same gesture.
  • Check the device logcat output for possible error messages. Usually a single gesture consists of hundreds of atomic steps. If any of these steps receives incorrect/unsupported parameters, then the whole gesture might fail. The log has details about each step being executed and arguments passed to it.
  • Make sure the gesture has valid coordinates and respects pauses between pointer state changes. For example, it is always mandatory to provide a valid element or valid absolute coordinates to any gesture at the beginning. Android only registers a long touch/click if the pointer has been depressed for longer than 500ms. For shorter actions, a simple click is registered instead.
  • Do not mix webview and native elements in actions arguments. Native actions can only consume native elements. One option for performing a native action on a web element would be to translate its coordinates into the native context (for example, using the mobile: viewportElementRect execute method), then pass these coordinates as native action arguments.

Check the below tutorials for more details on how to build reliable action chains:

  • Automating Complex Gestures with the W3C Actions API
  • Swiping your way through Appium by Wim Selles #AppiumConf2021
  • Android Input Events

docs.title: Webviews With Chrome Custom Tabs
docs.text:
Chrome custom tabs could have its own window handlings similarly to regular Selenium Web automation.

Appium allows switching the context from NATIVE_APP to WEBVIEW_xyz, for example, to interact with the WEBVIEW contents over chromedriver. Then, if the WEBVIEW uses Chrome's custom tabs implementation, the WEBVIEW context may require switching to a specific the window handler in order to interact with contents.

This approach may be useful if chrome://inspect or mobile: getContexts returns more available pages than actual contexts.

# Ruby
# Change the context to WebView (Attach to a chromedriver session)
driver.set_context('WEBVIEW_XYZ')

# Get available tabs/windows in the chrome instance
driver.window_handles

# Change the tab/window in the "chrome" instance
driver.switch_to.window('a window_handle name')

# interact with the tab/window

docs.title: Unlock
docs.text: UiAutomator2 driver allows dealing with the Android lock screen using various APIs. This article describes available APIs and their options.

docs.title: Unlock On Session Startup
docs.text:
UiAutomator2 provides the following capabilities to deal with the system lock screen:

  • appium:unlockStrategy
  • appium:unlockSuccessTimeout
  • appium:skipUnlock
  • appium:unlockType
  • appium:unlockKey

These capabilities could be used to unlock the device under test during the driver session initialization as well as deal with different lock screen types.

docs.title: appium:unlockStrategy
docs.text:
Either locksettings (default since Android 8/API level 26) or uiautomator (legacy).

The locksettings strategy uses adb shell locksettings CLI to deal with different types of device lock screens. It is fast, reliable, but has one downside: the actual pin, pattern or password must be temporarily removed in order to unlock the device and restored afterwards.

Setting the strategy to uiautomator will enforce the driver to use UiAutomator framework in order to interact with the device's lock screen for various unlock types. It might be slower and less stable in comparison to the locksettings strategy, although there is no other alternative if tests are being executed on an older Android version or the application under test requires the device to constantly maintain display lock settings.

docs.title: appium:unlockSuccessTimeout
docs.text: Maximum number of milliseconds to wait until the device is unlocked. 2000 ms by default

docs.title: appium:skipUnlock
docs.text: The appium:skipUnlock capability is enabled by default and makes the driver to detect and handle the lock screen upon session startup if it is present. If the lock screen cannot be detected upon session startup then nothing will be done. By default, it is assumed the device has a "simple" lock screen, which could be removed by waking up the device. In case the device has a different type of the lock screen configured in its settings then the information about it must be provided in the below capability values.

docs.title: appium:unlockType and appium:unlockKey
docs.text: This capability supports the following possible values:

docs.title: pin
docs.text: Assumes the device is protected with a PIN code. Expects the appium:unlockKey to contain a valid pin consisting of digits in range 0-9, for example 1111.

docs.title: pinWithKeyEvent
docs.text: Same as pin, but uses ADB instead of UiAutomator framework to enter the actual pin value.

docs.title: password
docs.text: Assumes the device is protected with a password. Expects the appium:unlockKey to contain a valid password consisting of latin characters, for example abcd1234.

docs.title: pattern
docs.text: Assumes the device is protected with a secret pattern. Check the example below for more details on the appium:unlockKey value for this particular unlock type.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Let say you have a device that is locked with a pattern similar to the one on the image below, and you want to run a test over that device.

We treat the pattern pins similarly to numbers on a digital phone dial. So, in this case the unlockKey is 729854163

and capabilities are:

{
  "appium:unlockType": "pattern",
  "appium:unlockKey": "729854163"
}

docs.title: Mid-Session Unlock
docs.text:
There is also a possibility to interact with the device's lock screen while the test session is running. Use the following mobile extensions for this purpose:

  • mobile: lock
  • mobile: unlock
  • mobile: isLocked
